IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r6.claim: ما may also be extra, as in the cited phrases from 23:40 and 17:110.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r6.anchor: و (ما) قد تزاد، كقوله: قال عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين (40) [المؤمنون: 40]

ITQAN:v4p345/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p345/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
ITQAN:v4p345/r4.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl finds the proverb “the best affairs are the middle” in the cow described as neither old nor young, balanced spending, neither constraining nor wholly opening one’s hand, and a middle volume of prayer.
ITQAN:v4p345/r4.anchor: فقلت إنك تخرج أمثال العرب والعجم من القرآن فهل تجد في كتاب الله ( خير الأمور أوساطها ) قال نعم في أربعة مواضع قوله تعالى ﴿ لا فارض

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Allāh and Raḥmān were both used as names of God among Arabs, and Raḥmān may have been more popular with the People of the Book.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Quraysh alleged that People of the Book helped the Prophet prepare the Qur’an, invoking the name Raḥmān as evidence; the author links this earlier accusation to 25:4.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They posited that some among the people of the Book help the Prophet (sws) in preparing this Book

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The opponents inferred from the name Raḥmān that the Prophet was trying to impose the People of the Book’s traditions and religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this person was trying to impose on them the traditions and religion of the People of the Book

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an answers that objection: bias toward a name should not prevent acceptance of truth, since God may be called by any name fitting His majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: bias towards a name should not be a cause of accepting the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an rejects bias against a divine name: God has several names, and any name befitting His majesty may be used.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God has several names and He can be called by every name that befits His majesty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The author suggests idolaters may have objected to Muslim prayer because their worship featured noise, clapping, and whistling, while Islamic prayer was solemn and dignified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: In their religion, making noise, clapping and whistling had a special status in worship

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is told to keep prayer and supplication at a moderate volume; this reflects the moderation expected of the Muslim community.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: since Muslims are a middle ummah, their prayers and supplications too should have moderation in them

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r2.claim: A report says Jews objected that Muhammad mentioned al-Rahman rarely although it was frequent in the Torah; this verse was revealed in response.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r2.anchor: روي أن اليهود قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r3.claim: Here calling means naming, not vocative invocation: Allah and al-Rahman are names for one essence, both permissible and leading to the same end.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r3.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى التسمية لا بمعنى النداء والمراد بالله والرحمن الاسم لا المسمى

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r4.claim: The beautiful names are good because they express holiness, praise, majesty, lordship, divinity, and supremely good acts.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r4.anchor: مستقلة بمعاني التقديس والتمجيد والتعظيم والربوبية والإلهية والأفعال التي هي النهاية في الحسن

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r5.claim: Another explanation says polytheists heard “O Allah, O Rahman” and accused Muhammad of worshiping two gods; the verse clarifies one essence, or permits using either name.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r5.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية حين سمع المشركون

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r6.speaker: المولى الفناري
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r6.claim: Al-Fanari distinguishes the divine name's lexical and usage specificity from al-Rahman's usage specificity, and calls Musaylima's title Rahman of Yamama deliberate unbelieving obstinacy.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r6.anchor: إن لاسم الجلالة اختصاصا وضعيا واستعماليا وللرحمن اختصاصا استعماليا

BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r7.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r7.claim: Al-Suhayli says Musaylima styled himself al-Rahman from before the Prophet's father was born, lived a long time, and was killed by Wahshi in Abu Bakr's caliphate.
BURSEVI:v5p163#2/r7.anchor: كان مسيلمة قديما يتكذب ويتسمى بالرحمن وقد قيل إنه تسمى بالرحمن قبل مولد عبد الله والد النبي

BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r1.claim: Loud prayer means reciting audibly in the Sacred Mosque, which provoked polytheists to insult the Qur'an, its sender, and its bearer; whispering would keep believers behind from hearing.
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r1.anchor: ذلك يحملهم على سب القرآن ومن أنزله

BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r2.claim: The wording omits “recitation,” since loudness and quietness describe sound rather than prayer's actions and remembrances; alternatively prayer names one part for the whole.
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r2.anchor: لأن الجهر والمخافتة صفتان تعتقبان على الصوت لا غير والصلاة أفعال وأذكار

BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashifi explains the instruction as not lowering the voice in recitation.

BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r4.claim: The requested course is a middle volume between the specified loudness and whispering, since the best matters are moderate.
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r4.anchor: أمرا وسطا فإن خير الأمور أوساطها

BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr whispered because he conversed privately with God, while Umar recited loudly to repel Satan and wake sleepers; the Prophet told each to adjust toward the middle.
BURSEVI:v5p164#2/r5.anchor: كان يخفت ويقول : أناجي ربي وقد علم حاجتي

BURSEVI:v5p165/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p165/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p165/r1.claim: The inward reading says prayer should be displayed enough to provide others with an example to follow.
BURSEVI:v5p165/r1.anchor: المتابعة والأسوة الحسنة {وابتغ بين ذالك سبيلا}

BURSEVI:v5p165/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p165/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p165/r2.claim: Specifically, obligatory prayers should be performed publicly in mosque congregations, while voluntary prayers are private at home.
BURSEVI:v5p165/r2.anchor: وهو إظهار الفرائض بالجماعات في المساجد وإخفاء النوافل وحدانا في البيوت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r1.claim: One occasion report says that in Mecca the Prophet invoked God as Allah and Rahman; polytheists accused him of worshipping two gods, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : صلى صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r2.claim: Another occasion report says People of the Book complained that the Prophet rarely mentioned Rahman although it appears often in the Torah, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r2.anchor: وعن الضحاك أنه قال : قال أهل الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r3.claim: For the polytheist occasion, the two names are equally names for one divine essence, so monotheism concerns the single worshipped entity; this coheres with the following denial of a child or partner.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r3.anchor: والمراد على الأول التسوية بين اللفظين بأنهما عبارتان عن ذات واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r4.claim: For the Jewish occasion, the names are equally apt for invocation; their preference for Rahman may reflect its frequent Torah mention. A proposed wisdom is that Moses' anger made abundant mention of mercy beneficial for his community.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r4.anchor: وعلى الثاني التسوية في حسن الإطلاق والإفضاء إلى المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r5.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r5.claim: He finds the Jewish occasion more fitting because describing the names as beautiful presupposes that listeners thought one name better than another.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r6.claim: He says the answer in both contexts is equality among the two names: one good name suffices against the Torah preference, and the names point to one perfect divine being rather than two gods.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r6.anchor: الغرض على الوجهين التسوية بين اللفظين في الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r7.claim: He distinguishes the complaints: Jews objected to preferring one name, while polytheists objected to combining them; أيا ما تدعوا fits the Jews if أو means choice and the polytheists if it permits both names.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#2/r7.anchor: ووجه الطيبي الأجوبية بأن اعتراض اليهود كان تعبيرا للمسلمين على ترجيح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r1.claim: He says the ideal direct answer to the Jews would have been that Allah is preferred because it gathers every perfection, unlike Rahman; if أو means permission, the verse instead directly permits the polytheists to combine names.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r1.anchor: إنما رجحنا الله على الرحمن في الذكر لأنه جامع لجميع صفات الكمال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r2.speaker: الجلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r2.claim: He argues that the fronted predicate فله الأسماء الحسنى means all names belong to God alone, answering the polytheist claim of multiple gods; since using both names is possible, he takes أو as permission rather than exclusive choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r2.anchor: ومنع الأجوبية أيضا الجلبي بأن تقديم الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r3.claim: He says any restriction focuses on the names' beauty rather than ownership, choice remains possible, and reason permits combining nonconflicting names; he sides with denying that the clause is the conditional answer and with reading أو as permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الحق مع مانع الأجوبية والقائل بالإباحة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r4.claim: He reads الدعاء as calling or invoking; al-Zamakhshari instead reads it as naming, with an omitted object and perhaps an omitted ب. The author reports objections about duplicate meanings or coordinating one divine referent with itself, and counters that the wording may name the names and that their distinct concepts suffice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r4.anchor: والدعاء على ما اختاره أبو حيان وجماعة بمعنى النداء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r5.claim: He sees al-Zamakhshari's naming interpretation as favoring the polytheist occasion; if the verse addresses polytheists it names God, while on a Jewish occasion it invokes God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r5.anchor: وجعل الطيبي لذلك تفسير الزمخشري إياه بالتسمية مؤذنا بميله إلى أنه رد على المشركين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r6.claim: أيا is a jussive conditional pronoun functioning as object, its tanwin replaces a genitive, and ما is emphatic or itself marks the condition; Talha ibn Musarrif reads من, parsed as extra or conditional, with two conditional particles together attested only exceptionally.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r6.anchor: اسم شرط جازم منصوب بتدعوا وجازم له فهو عامل ومعمول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r7.claim: An unattributed poetic line illustrates the rare combining of two prepositions that is compared to combining two conditional particles.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r7.anchor: فأصبحن لا يسألنني عن بما به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r8.claim: فله الأسماء الحسنى functions where the conditional answer belongs but gives its rationale instead, intensifying the point; the implied wording is that whichever name you invoke is good because God has the beautiful names.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r8.anchor: واقعة موقع جواب الشرط وهي في الحقيقة تعليل له

ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r9.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r9.claim: On the permission reading, calling God by either name is sound and using both is even better, as God commands invocation by the beautiful names; he reconstructs a concise or expanded conditional answer, which the author leaves as a strained account.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p191#3/r9.anchor: فبأيهما سميته فأنت مصيب وإن سميته بهما جميعا فأنت أصوب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r1.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r1.claim: A proposal to pause at أيا and treat ما تدعوا as an independent conditional clause is rejected: ما does not refer to rational individuals, and the condition would wrongly claim universal scope.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r1.anchor: على معنى أي اللفظين تدعوه به جاز

ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r2.claim: The pronoun in فله refers to the named or invoked entity understood from context, because names belong to their bearer rather than to a name or spoken title.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r2.anchor: عائد على المسمى أو المنادى المفهوم من الكلام والقرينة عقلية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r3.claim: The beautiful names denote the divine essence gathering all attributes of perfection, majesty, beauty, and generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r3.anchor: ووصف الأسماء بالحسنى لدلالتها على ما هو جامع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r4.claim: The Jews apparently accepted the beauty of God's other names but believed Rahman the most beloved, greatest, and noblest because it occurs frequently in the Torah; Muslims too recognize differences in rank among names.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p192/r4.anchor: إن الظاهر مما روي عن اليهود أنهم لا ينكرون حسن سائر أسمائه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet heard a man invoke God as the One, the Eternal Refuge who neither begets nor is begotten and has no equal, and swore that he had invoked by God's greatest name, which guarantees response.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r1.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك بأني أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت الأحد الصمد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r2.claim: Another report locates the greatest name in the verse naming God as one, without deity but Him, the Merciful, and in the opening of Al Imran naming the Living and Sustaining.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r2.anchor: اسم الله تعالى الأعظم في هاتين الآيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r3.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali says Allah is the greatest of the ninety-nine names because it denotes the essence containing all divine attributes and is uniquely exclusive to God; other names typically denote single qualities and can be applied to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r3.anchor: على أن الله أعظم الأسماء التسعة والتسعين لأنه دال على الذات الجامعة لصفات الإلهية كلها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r4.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r4.claim: He says Rahman is also exclusive to God and therefore close to Allah, though derived from mercy, explaining why the two are paired here; the honor of selected ninety-nine names reflects the dignity of their meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r4.anchor: واسمه تعالى الرحمن لا يسمى به غيره تعالى أيضا وهو من هذا الوجه قريب من اسم الله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r5.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r5.claim: Al-Razi says singling out Allah and Rahman implies they surpass other names, and putting Allah first signals its greater rank; this reading most directly answers the Jewish claim of a preferred name, though reports also rank names and may favor the polytheist occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r5.anchor: تخصيص هذين الإسمين يعني الله والرحمن بالذكر يدل على أنهما أشرف من سائر الأسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r6.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r6.claim: He argues that if God created injustice, an unjust act could yield a divine name, contradicting the claim that all divine names are beautiful; the author denies the entailment because creating something does not make it God's attribute or a proper name.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r6.anchor: واحتج الجبائي بالآية على أنه تعالى ليس خالق الظلم وإلا لصح اشتقاق اسم له سبحانه منه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r7.claim: Although God creates all things, reverence counsels against calling Him creator of the ugly; His name is Creator without qualification, or Creator of everything.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r7.anchor: نعم لا ينبغي أن يقال لله تبارك وتعالى خالق القبيح للزوم الأدب معه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r8.claim: A route through Nahshal ibn Sa'id and al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas is cited for calling this a protection verse, but the transmitted report is cut off before its content appears.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p193/r8.anchor: من طريق نهشل بن سعيد عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r1.claim: Reciting the verse at bedtime is said to protect a house from theft; a thief repeatedly gathered a migrant's belongings but could not open the door, and the owner said his house was protected.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r1.anchor: هو أمان من السرق وأن رجلا من المهاجرين تلاها حين أخذ مضجعه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r2.claim: In Mecca, while the Prophet was concealed, he recited aloud in prayer; polytheists cursed the Qur'an, its sender, and its bearer, so God instructed him to moderate his voice while remaining audible to companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r2.anchor: أخرج أحمد والبخاري ومسلم والترمذي والنسائي وابن حبان وغيرهم عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت ورسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r3.claim: Here prayer can stand metonymically for its recitation, one of its parts, or the phrase can mean the recitation of your prayer; recitation includes the basmala and other verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r3.anchor: وظاهره أن المراد بالصلاة القراءة التي هي أحد أجزائها مجازا ويجوز أن يكون الكلام على تقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r4.speaker: سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r4.claim: A report specifies the basmala: the Prophet raised his voice with it, and polytheists associated al-Rahman with Musaylima, then mocked with clapping and whistling; this reading especially fits the preceding verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r4.anchor:
أخرج ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف عن سعيد
قال : كان النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r5.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r5.claim: Abu Bakr prayed at night very quietly and Umar very loudly; after they reported their disagreement, the Prophet told Abu Bakr to raise his voice somewhat and Umar to lower his.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r5.anchor: ابن أبي حاتم عن الربيع قال : كان أبو بكر إذا صلى من الليل خفض صوته جدا وكان عمر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r6.claim: Asked why he prayed quietly, Abu Bakr said he was confiding in his Lord, who already knew his need.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r6.anchor: قيل لأبي بكر : لم تصنع هذا فقال : أناجي ربي وقد عرف حاجتي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r7.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r7.claim: Asked why he prayed loudly, Umar said the sound drove Satan away and awakened a sleepy person.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r7.anchor: وقيل لعمر : لم تصنع هذا قال : اطرد الشيطان وأوقظ الوسنان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r8.claim: Another explanation says not to make every prayer loud or every prayer quiet, but to recite aloud in some prayers such as Maghrib and Isha and quietly in others.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المعنى لا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها كلها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r9.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r9.claim: A report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections interprets prayer here as supplication; Mujahid and Ibn Abbas are also reported to hold this, with people loudly saying prayers such as “Have mercy on me.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r9.anchor: أخرج الشيخان وغيرهما عن عائشة قالت : إنما نزلت هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r10.claim: Bedouins from Banu Tamim loudly asked the Prophet for camels and children after his salutation, and the verse was revealed in response.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد أن أعرابا من بني تميم كانوا إذا سلم النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r11.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r11.claim: A second report interprets prayer as the tashahhud; Arabs reportedly recited their tashahhud loudly, prompting revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r11.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن عائشة أن الصلاة هنا التشهد وكان الأعراب كما نقل عن ابن سيرين يجهرون بتشهدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r12.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r12.claim: A literal interpretation of ritual prayer says do not pray for show or abandon prayer out of embarrassment; a similar interpretation is transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r12.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن عساكر عن الحسن أنه قال : المعنى لا تصل الصلاة رياء ولا تدعها حياء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r13.claim: Most commentators prefer Ibn Abbas's first explanation: the command concerns the volume of Qur'anic recitation in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r13.anchor: والأكثرون على التفسير المروي عنه أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r14.claim: Whispering means speech so quiet that the speaker cannot hear it; Ibn Masud says that anyone who makes his own ears hear has not whispered.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r15.claim: Calling moderation a path evokes a way toward which people direct themselves and by which capable travelers reach their goal; Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir and Abu Qilaba transmit that the best affairs are middle ones.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r15.anchor: والتعبير عن الأمر الوسط بالسبيل باعتبار أنه أمر يتوجه إليه المتوجهون ويؤمه المقتدرون

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r16.claim: Most commentators consider the verse still operative; one view calls it abrogated based on an Ibn Abbas report that the Meccan moderation rule lapsed after the Hijra.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r16.anchor: والآية على ما يقتضيه كلام الأكثرين محكمة وقيل منسوخة بناء على ما أخرجه ابن مردويه وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r17.claim: A proposed abrogation by the command to call upon God humbly and privately is dismissed as untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r17.anchor: وقيل هي منسوخة بقوله تعالى ( ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ) وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r18.claim: The rulings on reciting louder than needed and whispering in the defined sense are treated in fiqh works, to which readers are referred.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r18.anchor: حكم رفع الصوت بالقراءة فوق الحاجة وحكم المخافتة بالمعنى الذي سمعته المسطوران في كتب الفقه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r19.speaker: أبو رزين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r19.claim: Abu Razin transmits a codex reading attributed to Abd Allah: “Do not whisper your voice nor raise it.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p194/r19.anchor: ابن أبي داود في المصاحف عن أبي رزين قال قرأ عبد الله ( ولا تخافت بصوتك ولا تعال به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r13.claim: Esoterically, calling on Allah signifies annihilation in the divine essence, while calling on al-Rahman signifies annihilation in the attribute of mercy, the mother of attributes and the means by which God shows mercy to creatures.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r13.anchor: قيل دعاء الله بالفناء في الذات ودعاء الرحمن بالفناء في الصفة وصفة الرحمانية هي أم الصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r14.claim: Whichever of these two stations is sought, the beautiful names belong to God rather than the annihilated servant: the servant is absent in essence-annihilation, and the name al-Rahman is unique to God in attribute-annihilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r14.anchor: أيا ما طلبت من هذين المقامين ( فله ) تعالى في هذين المقامين ( الأسماء الحسنى ) لا لك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r15.claim: In the Futuhat, divine names belong both to Allah and al-Rahman, but Allah is invoked by a name's meaning and al-Rahman by its form; both forms ultimately signify the same meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r15.anchor: وفي الفتوحات المكية أنه تعالى جعل الأسماء الحسنى لله كما هي للرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r16.claim: The Breath of the Merciful manifests divine words in the void where the world appears; humans invoke God through the forms of names made from their breath and letter-combinations, serving as translators of the divine names.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r16.anchor: لأن الرحمن هو المنعوت بالنفس وبالنفس ظهرت الكلمات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r1.speaker: ابن عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r1.claim: The forms arising from the Merciful's breath have meanings behind them, like spirits behind letters; these meanings are divine-name realities beyond qualification and are related to the humanly uttered forms as meanings to letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r1.anchor: وخلف تلك الصور المعاني التي هي كالأرواح للأسماء الإلهية التي يذكر الحق بها نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r2.speaker: ابن عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r2.claim: The two permitted invocations are either the forms of merciful breath present in cosmic aspirations within our spirits, or the names articulated by our own breath as translation; one may attend to the meaning of Allah or the form of al-Rahman.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r2.anchor: فإن شئنا دعوناه بصور الأسماء النفسية الرحمانية وهي الهمم الكونية التي في أرواحنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r3.claim: The author says this difficult account does not make the verse's invocation a simple supplication in the earlier sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p198/r3.anchor: وهو كلام يعسر فهمه إلا على من شاء الله تعالى بيد أنه ليس فيه حمل الدعاء على ما سمعت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse followed the Prophet's tearful night prostration in Mecca, when he invoked Allah and al-Rahman and Abu Jahl accused him of calling on two gods; the two names belong to one God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ذات ليلة فجعل يبكي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r2.claim: The particle mā is extra in the construction, which means whichever of these two names, or any of God's names, you invoke, His are the beautiful names.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r2.anchor: {أيا ما تدعوا} "ما" صلة معناه: أيا ما تدعوا من هذين الاسمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r3.claim: Allah and al-Rahman are two names for the same God, not two deities.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p137/r3.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية (3) . ومعناه: أنهما اسمان لواحد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r1.claim: The same chain's added wording explains the middle course as letting companions hear the recitation without excessive loudness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r1.anchor: وبهذا الإسناد عن محمد بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا مسدد عن هشيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r2.claim: The middle course means letting companions hear the recitation without raising it so much that the Qur'an's opponents hear and abuse it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r2.anchor: أسمعهم ولا تجهر حتى يأخذوا عنك القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r3.speaker: عائشة والنخعي ومجاهد ومكحول
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r3.claim: They say the verse concerns supplication; Aisha specifically reports that it was revealed about prayerful invocation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: الآية في الدعاء وهو قول عائشة رضي الله عنها والنخعي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r4.claim: He says Bedouins of Banu Tamim loudly asked the Prophet for wealth and children after prayer, so the verse prohibited raising the voice in recitation or supplication.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن شداد: كان أعراب من بني تميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r5.claim: Mukhāfata means lowering the voice or silence, and the commanded course is between loudness and concealment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r5.anchor: والمخافتة: خفض الصوت والسكوت "وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا" أي: بين الجهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r6.claim: Abū Qatada reports the Prophet asking Abū Bakr to raise his quiet recitation a little and ʿUmar to lower his loud recitation a little: one said he was speaking to his Lord, the other waking sleepers and driving Satan away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p138/r6.anchor: عن أبي قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بكر: "مررت بك وأنت تقرأ وأنت تخفض

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r4.claim: The occasion may be that polytheists heard the Prophet say Allah and Rahman, then accused him of invoking another god; alternatively Jews said he rarely mentioned Rahman despite its prominence in the Torah.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r4.anchor: نزلت حين سمع المشركون رسول الله يقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r5.claim: One explanation makes the names equal in goodness of invocation and success in attaining the aim; Bayḍāwī prefers it in light of the following clause. The other equates their reference to one divine essence despite differing aspects of designation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r5.anchor: وعلى الثاني أنهما سيان في حسن الإطلاق والإفضاء إلى المقصود وهو أجود

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r6.claim: Here calling means naming: the first object is omitted, aw offers a choice, ayya’s tanwīn replaces its genitive complement, and ma reinforces its indefiniteness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r6.anchor: والدعاء في الآية بمعنى التسمية وهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين حذف أولهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to the named entity, not the name; the wording replaces an underlying statement that either call is good, emphasizing His beautiful names and their majestic and gracious attributes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r7.anchor: والضمير في { فله } للمسمى لأن التسمية له لا للاسم

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r8.claim: Do not recite loudly enough for polytheists to hear and revile the prayer, or so softly that fellow believers cannot hear; choose a middle course, since moderation is loved.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r8.anchor: بقراءة صلاتك حتى تسمع المشركين، فإن ذلك يحملهم على السب واللغو فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r9.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r9.claim: Abu Bakr whispered to privately address God who knew his need; Umar spoke aloud to repel Satan and wake sleepers, so the Prophet told Abu Bakr to raise his voice and Umar to lower his.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r9.anchor: روي أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كان يخفت ويقول: أناجي ربي وقد علم حاجتي، وعمر رضي الله عنه كان يجهر ويقول أطرد الشيطان

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r10.claim: Another interpretation prohibits making every prayer entirely loud or quiet, prescribing quiet recitation by day and loud recitation by night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:109-110/r10.anchor: لا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها بأسرها

QASHANI:17:107-110/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:107-110/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:107-110/r4.claim: Invoking Allah signifies annihilation in the all-comprehensive essence, while invoking al-Rahman signifies annihilation in the attribute that is the source of attributes; in either station the invoker's separate self disappears.
QASHANI:17:107-110/r4.anchor: بالفناء في الصفة التي هي أم الصفات

QASHANI:17:107-110/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:107-110/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:107-110/r5.claim: At witnessing, do not loudly claim prayer as your own and assert the self, or become so silent in annihilation that abiding and the possibility of following disappear; seek a just, steady way in multiplicity.
QASHANI:17:107-110/r5.anchor: يدل على الاستقامة ولزوم سيرة العدالة في عالم الكثرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r1.claim: Since learned believers abandoned inherited religions for the Qur'an, anyone with humanity should always call upon its revealer, not only in distress; prayer is especially apt in prostration with tears and humility.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r1.anchor: موجبا لكل من له أدنى إنسانية أن يؤمن به ويقبل عليه ويدعو من أنزله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r2.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, supporting supplication during prostration.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r2.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r3.claim: The imagined question from the Arab opponents is how to pray and which name to use; the all-encompassing name Allah signifies majesty, while al-Raḥmān suits this surah's repeated, worldly and otherworldly mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r3.anchor: ولما كان الجلالة هو الاسم الجامع لجميع معاني الأسماء الحسنى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r4.claim: Either name may be invoked because both name the same God: Allah expresses intrinsic majesty and al-Raḥmān beauty and beneficence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p437/r4.anchor: فاهتفوا بهذا الاسم الدال على الجلال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r1.claim: Both names refer to the one God, who alone owns all beautiful names denoting praise, glory, sanctification, and exaltation; the repeated pronoun is an emphatic rhetorical reuse.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r1.anchor: هذان الاسمان وغيرهما مما ورد عن النبي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes al-Raḥmān as God's encompassing mercy in creation from al-Raḥīm as mercy applied to particular people in ways suited to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r2.anchor: الرحمانية استغراق الخلق بالرحمة في إنشائهم , والرحيمية إجراء الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says no creature embodies al-Raḥmān's full, all-encompassing meaning, so this name belongs to God alone and its tawḥīd follows tawḥīd of the divine name; he links it to the names tradition from Abū Hurayra.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r3.anchor: فلم يجر بحق على أحد منهم , وإنما يوجد فيهم حظ خاص من معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r4.claim: Supplication is good at all times and especially in prayer; the prior references to dawn recitation and listening to Qur'an could suggest loud reading, so the verse sets its volume.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r4.anchor: أو سمى القراءة صلاة لأنها شرط فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r5.claim: Do not recite so loudly that hostile Quraysh hear and insult the Qur'an, God, and Muhammad, or so softly that companions behind cannot learn; use a middle course.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r5.anchor: فإن المخالفين قد عرف عنادهم فلا يؤمن سبهم للقرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports from the Prophet's hidden Meccan period: he recited loudly with companions, pagans heard and insulted, so God ordered a volume that companions could hear without alerting them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r6.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في هذه الآية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r7.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the verse was revealed concerning supplication; the author allows that it may have had multiple occasions of revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r7.anchor: وروى البخاري عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن هذه الآية نزلت في الدعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r8.claim: 'Prayer' names recitation here by referring to the whole for a part; earlier the part, dawn recitation, named the whole prayer because recitation was the focus.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p438/r8.anchor: أطلق هنا اسم الكل على الجزء إشارة إلى أن المقصود الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p347/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r7.claim: Aisha says the Prophet called on God aloud as Allah and Merciful, the Meccans heard and approached, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r7.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر بالدعاء فجعل يقول: يا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p347/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet prayed in Mecca calling Allah and Rahman; polytheists accused him of invoking two gods, prompting this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p347/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ذات يوم فدعا ربه فقال في دعائه: يا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p348/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r1.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai gives an occasion involving the Prophet in a field holding a palm branch, when Jews questioned the name Rahman; a priest in Yamama bore it, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم في حرث في يده جريدة فسأله اليهود عن الرحمن

DURR-FULL:v5p348/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r2.speaker: مكحول
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r2.claim: Makhul says the Prophet used Rahman and Rahim in prostration during night prayer in Mecca; a pagan associated Rahman with a man in Yemen, prompting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r2.anchor: عن مكحول: أن النبي كان يتهجد بمكة ذات ليلة يقول في سجوده: يا رحمن

DURR-FULL:v5p348/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r3.claim: A report through Ibn Abbas says reciting the verse before bed protects from theft; a thief could not leave with a householder's belongings, and the householder attributed his protection to the recitation.
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قول الله: {قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن

DURR-FULL:v5p348/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses whichever name you call as any of God's names, adding that God knows best.
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {أيا ما تدعوا} قال: باسم من أسمائه والله أعلم

DURR-FULL:v5p348/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command was revealed while the Prophet prayed secretly in Mecca but recited loudly; polytheists heard and abused the Qur'an, its sender, and its bearer.
DURR-FULL:v5p348/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} الآية قال: نزلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة متوار

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r1.claim: The instruction means not reciting so loudly that polytheists hear and abuse the Qur'an, nor so quietly that companions cannot hear and learn; seek a middle course.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r1.anchor: أي بقراءتك فيسمع المشركون فيسبوا القرآن {ولا تخافت بها} عن أصحابك فلا تسمعهم القرآن حتى يأخذوه عنك

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r2.claim: A further occasion report says loud recitation made the polytheists disperse, while quiet recitation prevented hidden listeners from hearing; the middle volume let a listener benefit.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جهر بالقرآن وهو يصلي تفرقوا عنه وأبوا أن يستمعوا

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's loud reading in Mecca caused harm, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر بالقراءة بمكة فيؤذي فأنزل الله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك}

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r4.claim: When the Prophet recited aloud at the House, polytheists harmed him, prompting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى عند البيت جهر بقراءته

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r5.claim: Another report says the Prophet and companions lowered their prayer after loud recitation angered polytheists; it links the instruction to 7:205's call to remember God inwardly.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى يجهر بصلاته فآذى ذلك المشركين

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person would raise his voice when supplicating in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قال: كان الرجل إذا دعا في الصلاة رفع صوته

DURR-FULL:v5p349/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas attributes the verse to Meccans associating the Prophet's loud basmala with Musaylima, who named himself Rahman.
DURR-FULL:v5p349/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان مسيلمة الكذاب قد تسمى الرحمن فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى فجهر ببسم الله

DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r1.speaker: سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r1.claim: Said says the Prophet recited the basmala aloud and that mockers associated Rahman with Musaylima, answering with clapping, gestures, and whistling; the verse followed.
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says loud Qur'an recitation drew abuse in Mecca; the verse instructs neither lowering the voice below one's own hearing nor excessive loudness, but a middle path. The Prophet left this practice after migration.
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جهر بالقرآن شق ذلك على المشركين فيؤذون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالشتم

DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakr explains that he recited quietly to converse privately with God, who already knows his need; after the verse he was told to raise his voice somewhat.
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.anchor: فقيل لأبي بكر رضي الله عنه: لم تصنع هذا قال: أناجي ربي وقد علم حاجتي

DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.claim: Umar explains that he recited loudly to drive away Satan and wake the sleeper; after the verse he was told to lower his voice somewhat.
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.anchor: وقيل لعمر رضي الله عنه: لم تصنع هذا قال: اطرد الشيطان وأوقظ الوسنان

DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas gives a parallel account: Umar urged Abu Bakr to raise his quiet night prayer while Abu Bakr urged Umar to lower his loud one; their report to the Prophet occasioned the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: كان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه إذا صلى من الليل خفض صوته جدا وكان عمر رضي الله عنه إذا صلى رفع صوته جدا

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r1.claim: The Prophet told Abu Bakr to raise his voice a little and Umar to lower his voice a little, establishing moderation.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r1.anchor: فأرسل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إليهما فقال: يا أبا بكر ارفع من صوتك شيئا

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r2.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r2.claim: Aisha reports that the instruction not to recite loudly or softly was revealed concerning supplication.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r2.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: إنما نزلت هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r3.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r3.claim: Aisha also reports that the verse was revealed concerning the tashahhud.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r4.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r4.claim: Aisha explains that the command concerns asking and supplication.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} قال: نزلت في المسألة والدعاء

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r5.claim: The Prophet supplicated aloud near the Kaaba, troubling the polytheists, and this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى عند البيت رفع صوته بالدعاء

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r6.claim: A report from an elderly Ansari Companion says the verse concerns supplication: do not publicize sins where listeners can mock them.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r6.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} إنما نزلت في الدعاء

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r7.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r7.claim: People loudly prayed, ‘O God, have mercy on me’; afterward they were told neither to whisper nor shout.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} قال: نزلت في الدعاء كانوا يجهرون بالدعاء

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r8.claim: Bedouins of Banu Tamim asked God for camels and children after the Prophet's prayer, occasioning the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد رضي الله عنه قال: كان أعراب من بني تميم إذا سلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: اللهم ارزقنا إبلا وولدا

DURR-FULL:v5p350/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r9.speaker: مجاهد رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r9.claim: Mujahid says the command concerns supplication and petition.
DURR-FULL:v5p350/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} قال: ذلك في الدعاء والمسألة

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r1.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r1.claim: Do not pray ostentatiously for people or abandon prayer from fear of them.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} ولا تصل مراياة الناس {ولا تخافت بها} قال: لا تدعها مخافة الناس

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r2.speaker: الحسن رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r2.claim: The verse forbids praying for show and abandoning prayer out of shyness.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r2.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قال: لا تصلها رياء ولا تدعها حياء

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r3.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r3.claim: Do not make all of the prayer audible or all of it private.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} لا تجعلها كلها جهرا {ولا تخافت بها} قال: لا تجعل كلها سرا

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r4.speaker: أبو رزين رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r4.claim: In Ibn Umar's reading, the phrase means neither lower the voice too much nor raise it excessively.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r4.anchor: عن أبي رزين رضي الله عنه قال: في قراءة عبد الله بن عمر {ولا تخافت} بصوتك ولا تعال به

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r5.claim: A whisper is not so low that the speaker cannot hear it himself.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: لم يخافت من أسمع أذنيه

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r6.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r6.claim: Knowledge is better than action; the middle course is best and virtue lies between two bad extremes, as the verse teaches.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r6.anchor: عن مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير قال: العلم خير من العمل وخير الأمور أوسطها والحسنة بين تلك السيئتين

DURR-FULL:v5p351/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r7.speaker: أبو قلابة
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r7.claim: The best matters are those in the middle.
DURR-FULL:v5p351/r7.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال: خير الأمور أوسطها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r1.claim: The choice between Allah and al-Raḥmān has a specific occasion, since otherwise there is no reason to single this attribute out over other beautiful names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r1.anchor: لا شك أن لنزول هذه الآية سببا خاصا إذ لا موجب لذكر هذا التخيير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Wāḥidī report that the Prophet invoked “O Merciful, O Compassionate”; polytheists accused him of calling two gods, and the verse allowed either name, implicitly including al-Raḥīm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r2.anchor: فأما سبب نزولها فروى الطبري والواحدي عن ابن عباس قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports that Abū Jahl heard the Prophet say “O Allah, O Merciful” and accused him of invoking another deity; Ibn Mardawayh transmits it, and the author finds it more apt to the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r3.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) : عن ابن عباس سمع أبو جهل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r4.claim: The occasion arose when the preceding verse was revealed; many divine names do not imply many divine beings, unlike worship of distinct entities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r4.anchor: والكلام رد وتعليم بأن تعدد الأسماء لا يقتضي تعدد المسمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r5.claim: Ay is originally interrogative; extra mā makes it conditional, so tadʿū is jussive and the answer begins with fa. The beautiful names permit invocation by any name because the referent is one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p235/r5.anchor: فإذا اقترنت بها ( ما ) الزائدة أفادت الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r1.claim: “Call upon Allah or al-Raḥmān” can mean mention either name in prayer; alternatively, it means name your Lord by either, with the first object omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r1.anchor: ومعنى { ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن } ادعوا هذا الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r2.claim: The prayer-volume instruction connects to the naming command and supports the occasion involving the Prophet's audible invocation of al-Raḥmān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r2.anchor: بسبب جهر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه باسم الرحمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r3.speaker: السلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r3.claim: Early authorities explained ṣalāt here as either supplication or formal prayer; those choosing formal prayer mean its recitation, which can be loud or quiet.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r4.claim: In either interpretation, the Prophet audibly invoked al-Raḥmān; some polytheists asked who it was or accused him of invoking two gods, while others insulted the Qur'an, Messenger, or al-Raḥmān as another lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r4.anchor: وعلى كلا الاحتمالين فقد جهر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بذكر الرحمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r5.claim: Opponents may have read public recitation as provocation; excessive loudness could inflame them and harden disbelief when the aim was to soften hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r5.anchor: فأمره الله تعالى بأن لا يجهر بصلاته هذا الجهر تجنبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r6.claim: The ban targets excessive loudness; the ban on whispering prevents secret or wholly silent prayer so potential converts can hear it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p237/r6.anchor: والمقصود من الكلام النهي عن شدة الجهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says polytheists heard Muhammad invoke Allah and al-Raḥmān and objected that he had ordered one god but prayed to two.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r3.anchor: سبب نزول هذه الآية أن المشركين سمعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r4.speaker: مكحول
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r4.claim: Makḥūl says a polytheist heard the Prophet invoke al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, mistook the name for a man in Yamāma, prompting the clarification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r4.anchor: وقال مكحول: تهجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r5.claim: Ṭalḥa reads ayyan mā tadʿū fa-lahu al-asmāʾ, meaning God has all other beautiful names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r6.claim: Divine names express best attributes and require revealed authorization, not independent reasoning; a report lists ninety-nine names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r6.anchor: وهي بتوقيف، لا يصح وضع اسم الله بنظر إلا بتوقيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r7.claim: Whichever name one invokes, it is the one God who possesses all beautiful names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r7.anchor: أي الأسماء تدعوا به فأنت مصيب له الأسماء الحسنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r8.claim: Absolute whispering is inaudible even to speaker, but here the command means lowering the voice without total silence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r8.anchor: هذه هي حقيقته، ولكنه في الآية عبارة عن خفض الصوت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r9.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وعائشة وجماعة: هي الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also takes ṣalāt as Qur'an recitation in prayer; loud recitation brought abuse, so the Prophet was told to use moderate volume audible to companions but not provoking polytheists.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r10.anchor: والسبب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جهر بالقرآن فسمعه المشركون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r11.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r11.claim: Ibn Sīrīn says the verse was revealed about Bedouins reciting tashahhud aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r11.anchor: قال ابن سيرين: كان الأعراب يجهرون بتشهدهم، فنزلت الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r12.claim: Abū Bakr recited quietly to privately supplicate; ʿUmar aloud to repel Satan and wake sleepers. Later Abū Bakr was told to raise his voice and ʿUmar lower his.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r12.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية، قيل لأبي بكر: ارفع أنت قليلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r13.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r13.claim: ʿĀʾisha also takes ṣalāt to mean tashahhud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r13.anchor: الصلاة» يراد بها في هذه الآية التشهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r14.claim: They say not to overdo loudness or ruin prayer by whispering, but to follow a middle way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r14.anchor: ولا تحسن صلاتك في الجهر ولا تسئها في السر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r15.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse rejects alternating loud and quiet practices of Gospel and Torah communities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r15.anchor: النهي عما يفعله أهل الإنجيل والتوراة من رفع الصوت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r16.claim: Another report says do not recite aloud in daytime prayers or whisper in night prayers, but follow the prescribed way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r16.anchor: ولا تجهر بصلاة النهار ولا تخافت بصلاة الليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says one who can make his ears hear has not whispered; the author calls it the basic linguistic sense, though the Abū Bakr report complicates it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491#3/r17.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود لم يخافت من أسمع أذنيه

SULAMI:v1p399#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r1.claim: No one invokes God except through faith; a true invocation is not attained in that way.
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r1.anchor: ما دعا الله أحد قط إلا إيمانا وإما دعوة حقيقة فلا

SULAMI:v1p399#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r2.claim: God's names cannot be counted, and His essence is not truly pointed to or described except by praise; the Real exceeds concepts and understanding, so predicates cannot contain Him.
SULAMI:v1p399#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : أسماؤه لا تدخل تحت الحصر ، وذاته ليس بمشار إليه ولا بموصوف حقيقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r1.claim: When the Prophet invoked the names al-Rahman and al-Rahim while prostrating at night in Mecca, polytheists thought he called two gods, identifying al-Rahman with Musaylima; this occasion prompted the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r1.anchor: فجعل يقول في سجوده يا رحمن يا رحيم فقال المشركون كان محمد يدعو إلها واحدا فهو الآن يدعو إلهين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r2.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran says Arabs questioned the unfamiliar name al-Rahman after the Prophet began writing basmala al-Rahman al-Rahim following 27:30.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r2.anchor: هذا الرحيم نعرفه فما الرحمن فنزلت هذه الاية قاله ميمون بن مهران

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says People of the Book asked why the Prophet mentioned al-Rahman so little when the Torah mentions it often.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r3.anchor: إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وقد أكثر الله في التوراة هذا الاسم فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r4.claim: The Prophet first recited aloud in Mecca; after the polytheists cursed the Quran and its messenger, he lowered his voice, but then companions could not hear him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r4.anchor: كان يرفع صوته بالقرآن بمكة فيسب المشركون القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r5.claim: Aisha reports that the verse was revealed when a Bedouin raised his voice during the tashahhud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r5.anchor: أن الأعرابي كان يجهر في التشهد ويرفع صوته فنزلت هذه الآية هذا قول عائشة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r6.claim: Muqatil says that at dawn prayer by al-Safa, Abu Jahl challenged Muhammad’s recitation; when the Prophet lowered his voice, Abu Jahl boasted that he had silenced him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r6.anchor: فجهر بالقرآن في صلاة الغداة فقال أبو جهل لاتفتر على الله فخفض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صوته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r7.claim: Invoking Allah or al-Rahman means choosing either name for the same God; any of God’s names may be invoked.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r7.anchor: إن شئتم فقولوا يا ألله وإن شئتم فقولوا يارحمن فانهما يرجعان إلى واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r8.claim: Al-Farra says mā in ayyāmā may be an extra particle, as in 23:40, or mean whichever, repeated because the two names have different forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p98#3/r8.anchor: وما قد تكون صلة كقوله عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين المؤمنون 40 وتكون في معنى أي معادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r1.claim: If salāt means ritual prayer, Ibn Abbas gives a reading-based interpretation: do not recite too loudly or too softly; calling recitation prayer has two grammatical explanations, including that it is part of prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r1.anchor: لاتجهر بقراءتك ولا تخافت بها فكأنه نهي عن شدة الجهر بالقراءة وشدة المخافتة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets the command as forbidding ostentatious prayer and abandoning prayer from fear of people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r2.anchor: لا تصل مراءاة للناس ولا تدعها مخافة الناس قاله ابن عباس ايضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r3.speaker: عائشة وابن سيرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r3.claim: A report from Aisha and Ibn Sirin says not to raise the voice in the prayer’s tashahhud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r3.anchor: لا تجهر بالتشهد في صلاتك روي عن عائشة في رواية وبه قال ابن سيرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r4.claim: Ikrima interprets the command as avoiding both conspicuous performance and excessive concealment of prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r4.anchor: لا تجهر بفعل صلاتك ظاهرا ولا تخافت بها شديد الاستتار قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says not to make prayer’s public form good while making its inward reality bad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r5.anchor: لا تحسن علانيتها وتسيء سريرتها قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r6.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla says to recite aloud in night prayer and quietly in day prayer, as commanded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r6.anchor: فاجهر في صلاة الليل وخافت في صلاة النهار على ما أمرناك به ذكره القاضي أبو يعلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r7.speaker: عائشة وأبو هريرة ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r7.claim: A second broad interpretation takes salāt here to mean supplication.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r7.anchor: أن المراد بالصلاة الدعاء وهو قول عائشة وأبي هريرة ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r8.claim: Mukhāfata means concealment or quietness; seek a middle course between loudness and quietness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r8.anchor: المخافتة الإخفاء يقال صوت خفيت وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا أي اسلك بين الجهر والمخافتة طريقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the command was abrogated by the instruction to remember God inwardly and quietly in 7:205.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r9.anchor: نسخت هذه الآية بقوله واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخفية ودون الجهر من القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r10.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r10.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says it was abrogated by the command to proclaim openly in 15:94.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r11.claim: The author considers abrogation here unlikely on closer examination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p100/r11.anchor: وعلى التحقيق وجود النسخ هاهنا بعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r1.claim: Against polytheists who reject God's attribute of mercy and the name al-Rahman, the verse says either name invokes the same God, who possesses the most beautiful names.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r1.anchor: أي: لا فرق بين دعائكم له باسم "الله" أو باسم (3) " الرحمن "، فإنه ذو الأسماء الحسنى،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r2.speaker: مكحول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r2.claim: Mak-hul reports that a polytheist heard the Prophet invoke al-Rahman and al-Rahim in prostration, thought he was invoking two gods, and the verse was revealed; Ibn Jarir also transmits it from Ibn Abbas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#2/r2.anchor: وقد روى مكحول (4) أن رجلا من المشركين سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول في سجوده: "يا رحمن يا رحيم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r1.claim: In Mecca, audible Qur’an prompted polytheists to insult the Qur’an, its revealer, and its messenger; the Prophet was told to recite moderately so companions could hear without provoking them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r1.anchor: حدثنا أبو بشر، عن (5) سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت (6) هذه الآية وهو متوار بمكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak adds that after the migration to Medina the restriction fell away, and the Prophet could recite in either manner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r2.anchor: وكذا روى (2) الضحاك عن ابن عباس، وزاد: "فلما هاجر إلى المدينة، سقط ذلك، يفعل أي ذلك شاء" (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits Ibn Abbas’s account that loud recitation drove opponents away, while quiet recitation prevented covert listeners from hearing; the middle course let them benefit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: حدثني داود بن الحصين، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r4.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r4.claim: Ikrima, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Qatada say the verse concerns recitation during prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r4.anchor: وهكذا قال عكرمة، والحسن البصري، وقتادة: نزلت هذه الآية في القراءة في الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says one should not whisper so softly that one cannot hear oneself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r5.anchor: وقال شعبة عن أشعث بن أبي سليم (9) عن الأسود بن هلال، عن ابن مسعود: لم يخافت بها من أسمع أذنيه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r6.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin reports Abu Bakr’s quiet recitation as intimate prayer and Umar’s loud recitation as repelling Satan and waking sleepers; both were praised, then each was told to moderate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p128#3/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: نبئت أن أبا بكر كان إذا صلى فقرأ خفض صوته، وأن عمر كان يرفع صوته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r1.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas’s view that the verse concerns supplication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r1.anchor: وقال أشعث بن سوار، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: نزلت في الدعاء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r2.claim: Aisha likewise holds that the verse concerns supplication, as transmitted by Sufyan and Malik through Urwa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r2.anchor: وهكذا روى الثوري، ومالك، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن عائشة: نزلت في الدعاء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r3.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وأبو عياض ومكحول وعروة بن الزبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r3.claim: Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, Abu Iyad, Makhul, and Urwa ibn al-Zubayr also say the verse concerns supplication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r3.anchor: وكذا قال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وأبو عياض، ومكحول، وعروة بن الزبير.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Shaddad reports that Bedouins of Banu Tamim asked for camels and children after the Prophet prayed, occasioning the verse about not raising or lowering the voice excessively.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال: كان أعراب من بني تميم إذا سلم النبي (12) صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r5.claim: Aisha says the verse concerns the tashahhud; Hafs from Ash‘ath ibn Sawwar and Muhammad ibn Sirin report the same interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r5.anchor: عن أبيه، عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، نزلت (1) هذه الآية في التشهد:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the instruction as forbidding ostentatious prayer and forbidding abandoning prayer from fear of people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قال: لا تصل مراءاة الناس، ولا تدعها مخافة الناس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says one must not make the outward prayer beautiful while corrupting the inward prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r7.anchor: عن الحسن البصري: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قال: لا تحسن علانيتها وتسيء سريرتها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the People of the Book whispered and then shouted letters while their followers shouted behind them; the verse prescribed the prayer practice taught by Gabriel between those extremes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p129/r8.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في قوله: {وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا} قال: أهل الكتاب يخافتون

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r1.claim: Takbīr means magnification; God is greater because He is powerful, knowing, living, hearing, seeing, eternal, wise, just, and transcendent.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r1.anchor: التكبير: التعظيم، ومنه: (فلما رأينه أكبرنه) وكبر الله وصفه بأنه أكبر من كل شيء،

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r2.claim: The particle ما in أياما may be extra, as in the cited Qur’anic phrase عما قليل.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r2.anchor: (ما) في قوله: (أيا ما) قيل: صلة كقوله: (عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين (40).

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r3.claim: Alternatively, ما may mean أي and repeat the sense for emphasis, meaning any thing.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r3.anchor: وقيل: (ما) بمعنى أي، كررت لاختلاف اللفظين للتأكيد تقديره: أي شيء،

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r4.claim: The singular تدعو is used because the clause is conditional; its answer is فله الأسماء الحسنى.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r4.anchor: وقال: تدعوا ولم يقل: تدعون لأنه محل مجازاة، وجوابه في الفاء التي في قوله: فله الأسماء الحسنى.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r5.claim: The verse followed a Meccan night prayer in which the Prophet invoked al-Rahman and al-Rahim, prompting polytheists to think he invoked two gods.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r5.anchor: قيل: تهجد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذات ليلة بمكة وكان يقول: يا رحمن يا رحيم، فقال المشركون: كان يدعو إلها واحدا والآن يدعو إلهين، فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r6.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r6.claim: Another report says polytheists recognized al-Rahim but claimed not to know al-Rahman.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r6.anchor: وقيل: قال المشركون: أما الرحيم فنعرفه، وأما الرحمن فلا نعرفه، فنزلت الآية، عن ميمون بن مهران.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r7.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r7.claim: A report says People of the Book objected that al-Rahman was mentioned rarely by the Prophet though often in the Torah.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r7.anchor: وقيل: قال أهل الكتاب: إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وهو كثير في التوراة، فنزلت الآية، عن الضحاك.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r8.claim: One occasion report says the Prophet’s raised prayer voice caused polytheists to abuse the Qur’an and its bearer.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r8.anchor: قيل: كان إذا صلى رفع صوته فمنعه المشركون وسبوا القرآن ومن جاء به ورموه، فنزلت الآية، عن سعيد بن جبير.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r9.claim: Another report says opponents objected to loud mosque recitation because it disturbed their idols and provoked them to curse God.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r9.anchor: وقيل: كان يجهر بالقرآن، فقالوا: لا تجهر بالقرآن في المسجد فتؤذي آلهتنا فنهجوا ربك، فنزلت الآية، عن سعيد بن جبير.

JISHUMI:v6p4330/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r10.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r10.claim: Muqatil locates the prayer near al-Safa; Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet, who lowered his voice and was mocked for it.
JISHUMI:v6p4330/r10.anchor: وقيل: كان يصلي في دار أبي سفيان بن الحارث عند الصفا ويجهر بقراءته، فمر به أبو جهل وقال: لا تفتر على الله، فخفض صوته،

AKHFASH:v2p426/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p426/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p426/r4.claim: أيا ما تدعوا is as though it said أيا تدعوا; the sense is whichever of the two invocations you make, God has the beautiful names.
AKHFASH:v2p426/r4.anchor: وقال {أيا ما تدعوا} كأنه قال "أيا تدعوا".

AKHFASH:v2p426/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p426/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p426/r5.claim: He explains this as asking which of the two names you call, since all the beautiful names belong to God.
AKHFASH:v2p426/r5.anchor: وقال {أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسمآء الحسنى} يقول: "أي: الدعائين تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى".

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Abu Jahl heard Muhammad say Allah and al-Rahman and objected that he forbade worshipping two gods yet called another deity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما سمعه أبو جهل يقول : يا الله يا رحمن ، فقال : إنه ينهانا أن نعبد إلهين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r2.speaker: author
