KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r2.claim: Another account says the People of the Book complained that Muhammad mentioned al-Rahman too little despite its frequent appearance in Torah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن أهل الكتاب قالوا : إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وقد أكثر الله في التوراة هذا الاسم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r3.claim: Calling on the names means naming God, not vocatively supplicating Him; the verb can take two objects, though one may be omitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r3.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى التسمية لا بمعنى النداء ، وهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين ، تقول : دعوته زيدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r4.claim: Allah and al-Rahman denote the names; whichever one is used, all the beautiful names belong to their referent, God Himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r4.anchor: والله والرحمان ، المراد بهما الاسم لا المسمى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r5.claim: The conjunction offers a choice of either name; tanwin in ayyā replaces its genitive complement and mā emphasizes the generality of which name is used.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r5.anchor: وأو للتخيير ، فمعنى { ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمان } سموا بهذا الاسم أو بهذا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r6.claim: The pronoun to Him refers to the named divine essence, not either name; the two names are beautiful because they express praise, sanctification, and greatness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r6.anchor: والضمير في { فله } ليس براجع إلى أحد الاسمين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r7.claim: Prayer here means its recitation by ellipsis; the Prophet raised his voice and pagans abused him, so he was told to lower it enough to avoid them but not hide it from followers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r7.anchor: بصلاتك بقراءة صلاتك على حذف المضاف ؛ لأنه لا يلبس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r8.claim: Abu Bakr prayed quietly, saying he was confiding in his Lord who knew his need; Umar prayed loudly to repel Satan and wake sleepers, so both were told to moderate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r8.anchor: وروي أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كان يخفي صوته بالقراءة في صلاته ويقول : أناجي ربي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r9.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r9.claim: Umar said that he raised his voice to repel Satan and wake the sleeper.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r9.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يرفع صوته ويقول : أزجر الشيطان وأوقظ الوسنان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r10.claim: Another interpretation says not to recite every prayer either loudly or quietly, but to recite night prayers aloud and daytime prayers softly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r10.anchor: وقيل : معناه ولا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها كلها ، وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r11.claim: Prayer may instead mean supplication; some scholars considered this verse abrogated by the command to call upon God humbly and privately.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r11.anchor: وقيل { بصلاتك } بدعائك . وذهب قوم إلى أن الآية منسوخة بقوله : { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r12.claim: Seeking a middle way is a figure for choosing a moderate manner of recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p654/r12.anchor: وابتغاء السبيل : مثل لانتحاء الوجه الوسط في القراءة

FARRA:v2p133/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p133/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p133/r1.claim: ما in أيًّا ما تدعوا may be extra, or may reinforce أيًّا because the two words have different forms.
FARRA:v2p133/r1.anchor: وقوله: أيا ما تدعوا [110] (ما) قد يكون صلة، كما قال تبارك وتعالى (عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين)

FARRA:v2p133/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p133/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p133/r2.claim: وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا means seek a moderate course.
FARRA:v2p133/r2.anchor: وقوله: (وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا) أي قصدا.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r1.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r1.claim: Al-Raḥmān occurred rarely in the Quran but often in the Torah; Jewish converts including Ibn Salam disliked its rarity and wished it were mentioned more.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r1.anchor: أحدهما : قاله الكلبي . أن ذكر الرحمن كان في القرآن قليلا وهو في التوراة كثير , فلما أسلم ناس من اليهود منهم ابن سلام وأصحابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r2.claim: When Muhammad prayed “O Raḥmān, O Raḥīm,” polytheists objected that he claimed one God while invoking two; the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r2.anchor: الثاني : ما قاله ابن عباس أنه كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ساجدا يدعو ( يا رحمن يا رحيم ) فقال المشركون

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r3.speaker: عائشة ومكحول
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r3.claim: Ṣalāt here can mean supplication: do not make supplication too loud or too quiet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أنه عنى بالصلاة الدعاء , ومعنى ذلك ولا تجهر بدعائك ولا تخافت به , وهذا قول عائشة رضي الله عنها ومكحول .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r4.claim: Ibrahim warns people who stare toward the sky during prayer that their eyes may not return to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r4.anchor: قال إبراهيم : لينتهين أقوام يشخصون بأبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة أو لا ترجع إليهم أبصارهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r5.claim: One view concerns ritual prayer recitation: in Mecca Muhammad recited so loudly that polytheists cursed him, so God ordered a moderate volume.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r5.anchor: أحدها : أنه نهى عن الجهر بالقراءة فيها لأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة كان يجهر بالقراءة جهرا شديدا ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r6.claim: Another view forbids reciting every prayer either aloud or silently: recite aloud at night and quietly by day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه نهى عن الجهر بالقراءة في جميعها وعن الإسرار بها في جميعها وأن يجهر في صلاة الليل ويسر في صلاة النهار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r7.speaker: ابن سيرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r7.claim: The instruction may forbid saying the tashahhud aloud during prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r7.anchor: الثالث : أنه نهي عن الجهر بالتشهد في الصلاة , قاله ابن سيرين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r8.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r8.claim: Ikrima says Muhammad prayed aloud in Mecca and Quraysh harmed him, so he whispered; God then ordered a middle course.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r8.anchor: الرابع : أنه نهي عن الجهر بفعل الصلاة لأنه كان يجهر بصلاته , بمكة فتؤذيه قريش , فخافت بها واستسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r9.claim: Hasan forbids showy public prayer paired with poor private prayer; one should neither pray ostentatiously nor abandon prayer from embarrassment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r9.anchor: الخامس : يعني لا تجهر بصلاتك تحسنها مرائيا بها في العلانية , ولا تخافت بها تسيئها في السريرة , قال الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r10.claim: The interpretation about moderating prayer’s volume is the clearest.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r11.claim: Abu Bakr lowered his voice to speak privately with God, who knew his needs; the Prophet approved. He also approved Umar’s loud voice to wake sleepers and drive Satan away, then told Abu Bakr to raise his voice slightly and Umar to lower his.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p280/r11.anchor: روي أن أبا بكر الصديق كان إذا صلى خفض من صوته فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لم تفعل هذا )

MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says one may invoke God by any of His names, for His are the most beautiful names.
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ أيا ما تدعوا ﴾ يقول بشيء من أسماء الله يقول بأي أسمائه تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى

MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r2.claim: Hasan says not to conceal the prayer in private.
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ يقول لا تخفها في السر

MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r3.claim: Mujahid says the instruction about neither raising nor lowering the prayer concerns invocation and petition.
MUJAHID:v1p371#4/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ في الدعاء والمسألة

MUQATIL:17:110-111/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r1.claim: A Muslim invoked Allah and al-Rahman in prayer; Abu Jahl objected that followers claimed one God but invoked two names.
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r1.anchor: ، وذلك أن رجلا من المسلمين دعا الله عز وجل، ودعا الرحمن في صلاته، فقال أبو جهل بن هشام: أليس يزعم محمد وأصحابه

MUQATIL:17:110-111/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r2.claim: One may call Allah or al-Rahman; either name is among God's beautiful names, including those at the end of al-Hashr.
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r2.anchor: { أيا ما تدعوا } ، يقول: فأيهما تدعو، { فله الأسمآء الحسنى } ، يعني الأسماء الحسنى التي في آخر الحشر،

MUQATIL:17:110-111/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r3.claim: At Mecca the Prophet recited aloud at dawn near Abu Sufyan's house by Safa; Abu Jahl threatened him, so he lowered his voice and mocked the change.
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r3.anchor: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بمكة يصلي إلى جانب دار أبي سفيان عند الصفا، فجهر بالقرآن في صلاة الغداة،

MUQATIL:17:110-111/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r4.claim: He should not recite loudly where polytheists could hear and harm him or so quietly companions cannot hear; choose the middle volume.
MUQATIL:17:110-111/r4.anchor: { ولا تجهر بصلاتك } ، يعني بقراءتك في صلاتك، فيسمع المشركون فيوءذوك، { ولا تخافت بها } ، يقول: ولا تسر بها،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r1.claim: On hearing the Prophet invoke Allah and al-Rahman, Abu Jahl objected that Muslims were forbidden two deities yet the Prophet invoked another.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r1.anchor: لما سمعه أبو جهل يقول يا الله يا رحمن قال انه نهانا أن نعبد آلهين وهو يدعو إلها آخر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r2.speaker: اهل الكتاب
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r2.claim: An alternative occasion says the People of the Book objected that the Prophet rarely mentioned al-Rahman although the Torah often did.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r2.anchor: وقيل أن اهل الكتاب قالوا انك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وقد اكثر الله في التوارة هذا الاسم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r3.claim: Here الدعاء means naming rather than calling; أو offers a choice between the two names or invocations.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r3.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى التسمية لا بمعنى النداء وأو للتخيير أي سموا بهذا الاسم أو بهذا أو اذكروا اما هذا واما هذا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r4.claim: In أيا ما, the tanwīn substitutes for a genitive complement, ما adds emphasis, and أيا is governed by تدعوا; either name may be used.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r4.anchor: والتنوين في ﴿ أيا ما تدعوا ﴾ عوض من المضاف اليه وما زيدت للتوكيد وايا نصب بتدعوا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r5.claim: The pronoun in فله returns to God’s essence and the fāʾ answers the conditional: whichever name is called, it is good.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r5.anchor: والضمير في فله يرجع إلى ذات الله تعالى والفاء لأنه جواب الشرط أي أياما تدعوا فهو حسن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r6.claim: The phrase explains that both names are good because they belong to God’s beautiful names, which express glorification, sanctification, and majesty.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r6.anchor: لأنه إذا حسنت أسماؤه كلها حسن هذان الاسمان لأنهما منها ومعنى كونها أحسن الاسماء أنها مستقلة بمعانى التمجيد والتقديس والتعظيم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r7.claim: ‘Prayer’ here means Qur’an recitation, with a complement omitted; this is clear because loudness and whispering apply to voice, whereas prayer includes actions and words.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r7.anchor: بقراءة صلايك على حذف المضلف لأنه لا يلبس اذ الجهر والمخافته تعتقبان على الصوت لا غير والصلاة أفعال وأذكار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r8.claim: The Prophet raised his recitation, so the polytheists heard, babbled, and cursed; he was told not to recite loudly enough for them to hear.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته بقراءته فاذا سمعها المشركون لغوا وسبوا فأمر بأن يخفض من صوته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r9.claim: Do not lower the voice so much that those behind the worshipper cannot hear; seek a middle level between loudness and whispering.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r9.anchor: ﴿ ولا تخافت بها ﴾ حتى تسمع من خلفك ﴿ وابتغ بين ذلك ﴾ بين الجهر والمخافتة ﴿ سبيلا ﴾ وسطا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r10.claim: Another reading is not to be loud or quiet in every prayer: recite aloud in night prayer and quietly in day prayer, or understand prayer as supplication.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p304/r10.anchor: أو معناه لا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها كلها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا بأن تجهر بصلاة الليل وتخافت بصلاو النهار أو بصلاتك بدعائك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r1.claim: Tukhāfit means to lower or soften the voice; seek a moderate path between reciting aloud and concealing it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r1.anchor: {ولا تخافت بها} أي لا تخفها. {وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا} أي بين الجهر وبين الإخفاء طريقا قصدا وسطا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r2.claim: Tartīl is clear, measured recitation that separates one letter from the next; related usage describes spaced or even teeth and articulated speech.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r2.anchor: والترتيل (3) في القراءة: التبيين لها. كأنه يفصل بين الحرف والحرف، ومنه قيل: ثغر رتل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r3.claim: A man with spaced teeth is called ratl, with kasrah on the first consonant.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p262#3/r3.anchor: ورجل رتل – بالكسر – بين الرتل: إذا كان مفلج الأسنان

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r1.claim: One occasion report says polytheists heard Muhammad invoke Allah and al-Rahman and accused him of calling on two gods despite preaching one.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r1.anchor: أن المشركين سمعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو «يا ألله يا رحمن» فقالوا:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r2.speaker: مكحول
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r2.claim: Makhul says the Prophet invoked al-Rahman and al-Rahim at night; a listener associated al-Rahman with a man in Yamama, prompting the verse to clarify that Allah and al-Rahman name one deity.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r2.anchor: تهجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة فقال في دعائه: «يا رحمن يا رحيم»

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r3.claim: Another occasion links the verse to the basmala: Quraysh recognized al-Rahim but asked who al-Rahman was after Muhammad wrote the formula.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r3.anchor: فكتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» فقال المشركون: هذا الرحيم نعرفه

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r4.claim: Another report says Jews asked why the Quran lacked the name al-Rahman, familiar from the Torah.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن اليهود قالت: ما لنا لا نسمع في القرآن اسما هو في التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r5.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads 'whichever you call' with man after ayyan, emphasizing that the Most Beautiful Names entail the finest attributes and meanings.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «أيا من تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى»

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r6.claim: God's names are established by revelation or consensus; reason alone cannot invent a name for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r6.anchor: وهي بتوقيف لا يصح وضع اسم الله بنظر إلا بتوقيف من القرآن أو الحديث أو الإجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r7.claim: The first setting says the Prophet prayed loudly with companions in Mecca, so polytheists heard and insulted the Quran, its sender, and its bearer; he was told to be audible to companions without exposing the recitation to opponents.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r7.anchor: نزلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوار بمكة، وكان إذا صلى بأصحابه رفع صوته بالقرآن،

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites the report as transmitted by Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and others, with Muslim's wording; khafata means lowering the voice or becoming still.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110/r8.anchor: أخرجه البخاري ومسلم والترمذي وغيرهم. واللفظ لمسلم. والمخافتة: خفض الصوت والسكون

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r1.claim: A poem is cited to illustrate khafata as a quiet breath or fading voice, and a faint or altered gaze.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r1.anchor:
لم يبق إلا نفس خافت
ومقلة إنسانها باهت

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r2.claim: Aisha says the instruction about not raising or lowering the prayer was revealed concerning supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r2.anchor: ما رواه مسلم أيضا عن عائشة في قوله عز وجل: { ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r3.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin's report about raised tashahhud implies that the verse calls for concealing it; Ibn Masud calls concealment the Sunna according to Ibn al-Mundhir.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r3.anchor: قلت: وعلى هذا فتكون الآية متضمنة لإخفاء التشهد، وقد قال ابن مسعود: من السنة أن تخفي التشهد

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr recited quietly to converse privately with God, while Umar recited aloud to drive Satan away and wake sleepers; the verse directed Abu Bakr to raise his voice a little and Umar to lower his.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r4.anchor: يسر قراءته، وكان عمر يجهر بها،

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r5.claim: On the day-versus-night interpretation, optional prayers may be recited aloud or quietly at any time, while obligatory prayers have established recitation rules.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r5.anchor: فأما النوافل فالمصلي مخير في الجهر والسر في الليل والنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r6.claim: Hasan interprets the command as prohibiting ostentation in public while also forbidding neglect in private.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: يقول الله لا ترائي بصلاتك تحسنها في العلانية ولا تسيئها في السر.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas also says not to pray for show or abandon prayer from fear of people.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لا تصل مرائيا للناس ولا تدعها مخافة الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r8.claim: Prayer is used for recitation and recitation for prayer by metonymy, since the prayer includes reciting, bowing, and prostrating; the sound hadith on dividing prayer refers to reciting al-Fatiha.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:110#2/r8.anchor: لأن الصلاة تشتمل على قراءة وركوع وسجود فهي من جملة أجزائها

MAJAZ:v1p392/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p392/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p392/r5.claim: ولا تخافت is like لا تخفت: do not whisper or voice it aloud, but let yourself hear it; Arabs use this in the daytime prayer, called العجما, and the source says it has not heard this for night prayer.
MAJAZ:v1p392/r5.anchor: «ولا تخافت بها» (110) مجازه: لا تخفت بها، ولا تفوه بها، ولكن أسمعها نفسك ولا تجهر بها فترفع صوتك

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads Allah and al-Rahman as alternative names, not different referents; either name is good because both belong to the beautiful names of one divine essence.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) المراد بهما الاسم لا المسمى والواو للتخيير بمعنى : { ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمان }

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r2.claim: On al-Kashshaf's grammatical reading, ayyan's tanwin compensates for a genitive, mā reinforces ambiguity, and the pronoun in fa-lahu refers to God Himself.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r2.anchor: والتنوين في { أيا } عوض عن المضاف إليه و { ما } صلة للإبهام المؤكد لما في أي

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r3.claim: God's names are beautiful because they convey praise and sanctification; Razi notes this was treated at length under 7:180.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r3.anchor: ومعنى حسن أسماء الله كونها مفيدة لمعاني التحميد والتقديس وقد سبق الاستقصاء في هذا الباب في آخر سورة الأعراف

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r4.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi argues that if God created injustice, He could be called unjust, contradicting the verse's assertion that all His names are beautiful.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r4.anchor: واحتج الجبائي بهذه الآية فقال : لو كان تعالى هو الخالق للظلم والجور لصح أن يقال يا ظالم

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r5.claim: Razi rejects the inference: creating movement or color does not make God movable or colored, and the same distinction blocks calling the creator of acts unjust.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r5.anchor: لا نسلم أنه لو كان خالقا لأفعال العباد لصح وصفه بأنه ظالم وجائر كما أنه لا يلزم من كونه خالقا للحركة

RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r6.claim: Even if calling God creator of ugly things is true, decorum favors invoking Him as Creator of heaven and earth rather than with distasteful descriptions.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59/r6.anchor: وكما أنكم تقولون أن ذلك حق في نفس الأمر ولكن الأدب أن يقال يا خالق السموات والأرض فكذا قولنا هنا

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says the Prophet raised his recitation and the polytheists cursed God and His messenger; revelation ordered a middle volume so companions could hear.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r1.anchor: الأول : روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته بالقراءة

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.claim: A report says Abu Bakr recited quietly to commune with God, while ʿUmar recited loudly to repel Satan and wake sleepers; the Prophet told each to moderate his volume.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r2.anchor: القول الثاني : روى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف بالليل على دور الصحابة ، وكان أبو بكر يخفي صوته بالقراءة

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.claim: A third view forbids making all prayer loud or all prayer soft, taking the middle path as reciting night prayers aloud and daytime prayers quietly.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r3.anchor: معناه : { ولا تجهر بصلاتك } كلها { ولا تخافت بها } كلها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا بأن تجهر بصلاة الليل

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.speaker: عائشة وأبو هريرة ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.claim: Aisha, Abu Hurayra, and Mujahid say prayer here means supplication; a transmitted Prophetic explanation warns against loud petitions that expose sins, while moderation means making oneself hear, as Ibn Masʿud says.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r4.anchor: والقول الرابع : أن المراد بالصلاة الدعاء وهذا قول عائشة رضي الله عنها وأبي هريرة ومجاهد قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها هي في الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the instruction as not displaying righteous acts in public while behaving badly in private.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r5.anchor: والقول الخامس : قال الحسن لا تراه بعلانيتها ولا تسىء بسريتها .

RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r6.claim: Prayer comprises acts and words, but loudness and softness concern sound, so the intended part is recitation and remembrance, using the whole term for a part.
RAZI-FULL:v21p59#2/r6.anchor: الصلاة عبارة عن مجموع الأفعال والأذكار والجهر والمخافتة من عوارض الصوت

RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r1.claim: Khafata means a voice weakens or settles; it can also describe low speech, death, withering crops, or people whispering together.
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r1.anchor: يقال خفت صوته يخفت خفتا وخفوتا إذا ضعف وسكن وصوت خفيت أي خفيض

RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r2.claim: The middle course fits the rule that both extremes are blameworthy; verses on a balanced community, moderate spending, and measured giving illustrate the principle.
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r2.anchor: وأقول ثبت في كتب الأخلاق أن كلا طرفي الأمور ذميم والعدل هو رعاية الوسط ولهذا المعنى مدح الله هذه الأمة

RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r3.claim: Some say the instruction was abrogated by the command to call upon God humbly and privately; Razi considers that view remote.
RAZI-FULL:v21p60/r3.anchor: ومنهم من قال الآية منسوخة بقوله : { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية } ( الأعراف : 55 ) وهو بعيد

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r1.claim: God and al-Raḥmān are both divine names; al-Raḥmān is a name of the Essence and also functions as a proper name.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r1.anchor: the latter, one of the most important Names of God, is considered a Name pertaining to the Divine Essence

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r2.speaker: Bḍ, IK
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r2.claim: One report says the verse followed idolaters hearing the Prophet call on Allah and al-Raḥmān, then accuse him of invoking two gods.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r2.anchor: invoking two separate Divine beings (Bḍ, IK)

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r3.speaker: Bḍ, IK
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r3.claim: Another account has the Prophet call al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, prompting the same accusation; the verse clarifies the names refer to one God.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r3.anchor: invoking two separate Divine beings (Bḍ, IK)

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r4.claim: The Most Beautiful Names are mentioned elsewhere, and their significance spans Muslim belief, practice, and piety.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r4.anchor: The mention of God’s Most Beautiful Names is also found in 7:180; 20:8; 59:24.

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r5.claim: Prayer should avoid loudness and show reverence and humility; some connect this with commands not to raise voices before the Prophet during prayer.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r5.anchor: One should be not loud in . . . prayer (see also 7:205), but rather demonstrate reverence and humility when praying

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r6.speaker: Bḍ, IK
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r6.claim: Some say quiet recitation protects the sacred prayer from idolaters overhearing and cursing or disparaging it.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r6.anchor: the idolaters overhear the prayer and respond by cursing or disparaging the sacred act (Bḍ, IK).

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r7.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r7.claim: Prayer should not be too quiet, so that beneficiaries can hear; an imam must be audible to those behind him.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r7.anchor: the imām, or prayer leader, should not recite so quietly that it is inaudible to those praying behind him (Bḍ).

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r8.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r8.claim: One report applies the instruction to personal supplication, although ṣalāh usually means canonical prayer.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r8.anchor: this injunction pertains to personal supplicatory prayer (duʿāʾ), although the verse uses ṣalāh, which usually designates the canonical prayer (IK).

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r9.claim: The middle way in prayer reflects Quranic moderation, the middle community, and the straight path.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r9.anchor: One should seek a way between is consistent with the Quran’s exhortation toward moderation in other matters

STUDYQURAN:17:110/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r10.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r10.claim: He says one should avoid loud prayer as ostentation and quiet prayer out of fear of others.
STUDYQURAN:17:110/r10.anchor: According to Ibn ʿAbbās, one should not pray loudly, so as to make an ostentatious display for other people, or too quietly, out of fear of them (IK).

NAHHAS:v2p443/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r15.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v2p443/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash Said interprets أيا ما تدعوا as ‘whichever of the two invocations you make.’
NAHHAS:v2p443/r15.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد : أي أي الدعاءين تدعو

NAHHAS:v2p443/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r16.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v2p443/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s interpretation, as transmitted by Abū Jaʿfar, is that either name—‘O God’ or ‘O Merciful’—may be invoked.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r16.anchor: قال أبو جعفر : وهذا قول الحسن أي إن قلتم يا الله يا رحمن

NAHHAS:v2p443/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r17.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p443/r17.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the phrase means whichever names you call upon, since God has the most beautiful names, including the listed names.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r17.anchor: وقال أبو اسحاق : المعنى أي الأسماء تدعون ^ ( فله الأسماء الحسنى ) ^

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r1.claim: Quraysh had rejected the name al-Rahman, so the Prophet is told that either name invokes the one God, who has the most beautiful names.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r1.anchor: بأي أسمائه جل جلاله تدعون ربكم، فإنما تدعون واحدا، وله الأسماء الحسنى

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that while the Prophet prostrated and called on al-Rahman and al-Rahim, the polytheists thought he invoked two gods; the verse answered them.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ساجدا يدعو: «يا رحمن يا رحيم»

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r3.speaker: مكحول
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r3.claim: Makhul reports that a Meccan heard the Prophet call on al-Rahman during night worship and mistook the name for a man of Yamama called al-Rahman.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r3.anchor: عن مكحول، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتهجد بمكة ذات ليلة، يقول في سجوده: «يا رحمن يا رحيم»

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses أيا ما تدعوا as calling God by any one of His names.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {أيا ما تدعوا} [الإسراء: 110] بشيء من أسمائه

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God has ninety-nine names in the Quran and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r5.anchor: عن مكحول، عن عراك بن مالك، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما كلهن في القرآن

TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r6.claim: The particle ما in أيا ما has two possible grammatical functions: an extra particle or a particle meaning in, repeated for varied wording.
TAB-FULL:v15p123#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: ولدخول «ما» في قوله {أيا ما تدعوا} [الإسراء: 110] وجهان: أحدهما أن تكون صلة

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r1.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r1.claim: One reported interpretation takes الصلاة here to mean supplication, so the Prophet should neither call loudly nor whisper it.

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r2.claim: Aisha says the prohibition concerns supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r2.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن عائشة، في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قالت: في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says people used to call out in supplication and were instructed not to be either loud or inaudible.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تعالى: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: كانوا يجهرون بالدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r4.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r4.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports from Aisha that the verse was revealed about supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r4.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء عن عائشة، قالت: نزلت في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r5.speaker: أبو عياض
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r5.claim: Abu ʿIyad identifies the prayer in the verse as supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r5.anchor: عن أبي عياض، في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r6.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r6.claim: A report from Ata says the verse was revealed about supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r6.anchor: عن عطاء، {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: نزلت في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p126/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r7.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p126/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في الآية: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r1.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns supplication and asking God.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] في الدعاء والمسألة

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr interprets the prayer as supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r3.claim: Abd Allah ibn Shaddad reports that after the Prophet’s greetings some Bedouins asked God for camels and children, and this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد، قال: كان أعراب إذا سلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: اللهم ارزقنا إبلا وولدا

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r4.speaker: هشام بن عروة
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r4.claim: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa transmits from his father that the verse concerns supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the phrase as supplication and asking God.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولا تجهر بصلاتك} [الإسراء: 110] . . الآية، قال: في الدعاء والمسألة

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r6.speaker: مكحول
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r6.claim: Makhul likewise says the instruction is about supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r6.anchor: عن مكحول، {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: ذلك في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r7.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says loud Quran recitation in prayer let the polytheists hear and insult the Quran, its revealer, and its messenger; the Prophet should not be so loud that they hear or so quiet that companions cannot.
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: نزلت هذه الآية ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوار

TAB-FULL:v15p129/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r8.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v15p129/r8.claim: A second interpretation takes الصلاة as ritual prayer and the prohibited loudness as Quran recitation.

TAB-FULL:v15p130/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak’s report from Ibn Abbas says loud Quran recitation in Meccan prayer made the polytheists abuse the Prophet; he should recite audibly enough for himself but not so loudly that they hear, and use a middle volume. The restriction ended after the Hijra.
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، إذا جهر بالصلاة بالمسلمين بالقرآن

TAB-FULL:v15p130/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet in Mecca should avoid both a voice heard by the enemy and a whisper inaudible to Muslims behind him.
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] . . الآية، هذا ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

TAB-FULL:v15p130/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r3.claim: In another report, loud recitation prompted the polytheists to curse the Quran and its messenger, while quiet recitation kept the Companions from hearing; the verse sets a middle course.
TAB-FULL:v15p130/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته بالقرآن، فكان المشركون إذا سمعوا صوته سبوا القرآن

TAB-FULL:v15p131/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says loud prayer caused listeners to disperse, while quiet prayer hid the recitation from people secretly trying to hear; the middle volume could let them benefit without exposing them to harm.
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جهر بالقرآن وهو يصلي تفرقوا

TAB-FULL:v15p131/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r2.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r2.claim: Saʿid reports that Quraysh asked the Prophet not to recite aloud in the Sacred Mosque lest their idols be harmed, threatening to insult his Lord, and the verse followed.
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r2.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر بقراءة القرآن في المسجد الحرام، فقالت قريش

TAB-FULL:v15p131/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r3.claim: A further Ibn Abbas report links the verse to the Prophet’s concealment in Mecca: loudness brought insults, but whispering prevented companions from hearing.
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مختف بمكة

TAB-FULL:v15p131/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explicitly identifies الصلاة in this reading as Quran recitation.
TAB-FULL:v15p131/r4.anchor: عن جعفر بن إياس، عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: في القراءة

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the Prophet’s loud voice pleased his Companions but led polytheists who heard it to insult him, prompting the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r1.anchor: عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، في هذه الآية {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا رفع صوته

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r2.claim: Abu Bakr says he lowered his voice in prayer to speak privately with his Lord, who already knew his need.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r2.anchor: فقال: أناجي ربي، وقد علم حاجتي

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r3.speaker: عمر
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r3.claim: Umar says he raised his voice to drive away Satan and wake the drowsy; after the verse, Abu Bakr was told to raise his voice a little and Umar to lower his.

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r4.claim: Ata reports disagreement over whether the verse concerns ritual prayer or supplication.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r4.anchor: عن عطاء، في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: يقول ناس إنها في الصلاة، ويقول آخرون إنها في الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r5.claim: Qatada says that in Mecca the Prophet was abused when polytheists heard him, so he was told to lower his voice and keep prayer between himself and God; what one’s ears hear is not a whisper.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا} [الإسراء: 110] وكان نبي الله وهو بمكة

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r6.claim: Qatada also says the Prophet should not raise his voice and be abused or recite so quietly that it becomes a whisper.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته بالصلاة

TAB-FULL:v15p133/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r7.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r7.claim: Aisha says the verse concerns the tashahhud in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p133/r7.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن عائشة، قالت: نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد

TAB-FULL:v15p134/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r1.speaker: ابن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r1.claim: Ibn Sirin transmits that an Arab recited the tashahhud aloud, and the verse was revealed concerning that practice.
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r1.anchor: عن أشعث، عن ابن سيرين، مثله. وزاد فيه: وكان الأعرابي يجهر فيقول: التحيات لله

TAB-FULL:v15p134/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r2.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r2.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say the Prophet and his Companions first recited aloud in Mecca, which bothered polytheists, so they concealed prayer; the verse moderates this. They link it to the command to remember God inwardly in 7:205.
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، والحسن البصري، قالا: قال في بني إسرائيل {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا} [الإسراء: 110]

TAB-FULL:v15p134/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the verse ethically: do not perform prayer publicly for show or hide it privately as wrongdoing; seek a middle way.
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، أنه كان يقول: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] أي لا تراء بها علانية

TAB-FULL:v15p134/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r4.claim: Al-Hasan further says not to make prayer’s public appearance beautiful while corrupting its inward reality.
TAB-FULL:v15p134/r4.anchor: كان الحسن يقول في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: لا تحسن علانيتها، وتسيء سريرتها

TAB-FULL:v15p135/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to pray ostentatiously or abandon prayer out of fear.
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] قال: لا تصل مراءاة الناس ولا تدعها مخافة

TAB-FULL:v15p135/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the middle way is the prayer Jibril taught the Muslim community, avoiding both the loud style of People of the Book and their whispering.
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا} [الإسراء: 110] قال: السبيل بين ذلك الذي سن له جبرائيل

TAB-FULL:v15p135/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the report from Ibn Abbas transmitted by Saʿid: recite and supplicate at a middle volume so Companions can hear without provoking the polytheists; it has the soundest Companion chain and best fits context.
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة، ما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس في الخبر الذي رواه أبو جعفر، عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v15p135/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r4.claim: The verse addresses Quran recitation, supplication, asking God, and remembrance in prayer; choose a voice audible to Companions but not the hostile polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v15p135/r4.anchor: ولا تجهر يا محمد بقراءتك في صلاتك ودعائك فيها ربك ومسألتك إياه، وذكرك فيها

TAB-FULL:v15p137/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r1.claim: A possible alternative would reserve quiet recitation for daytime prayers and loud recitation for night prayers, but al-Tabari rejects it because exegetical authorities unanimously disagree.
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r1.anchor: لكان وجها يحتمله التأويل أن يقال: ولا تجهر بصلاتك التي أمرناك بالمخافتة بها، وهي صلاة النهار

TAB-FULL:v15p137/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r2.claim: When asked what intermediate recitation is, Abd Allah says that one who makes his own ears hear is not whispering.
TAB-FULL:v15p137/r2.anchor: عن الأسود بن هلال، قال: قال عبد الله: لم يخافت من أسمع أذنيه

TABATABAI:17:107-110/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:107-110/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:107-110/r7.claim: Calling upon Allah or al-Raḥmān is equally permissible: the alternatives name the one God, rather than two distinct beings.
TABATABAI:17:107-110/r7.anchor: فالمراد بقوله { الله } و { الرحمن } الاسمان الدالان على المسمى دون المسمى

TABATABAI:17:110/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:110/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:110/r1.claim: Ayyan is conditional and the object of tadʿū; mā is emphatic, while the answer clause places the cause where the consequence is meant.
TABATABAI:17:110/r1.anchor: و { أيا } شرطية وهي مفعول { تدعوا }. وقوله { فله الأسماء الحسنى } جواب الشرط

TABATABAI:17:110/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:110/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:110/r2.claim: Every name of God is beautiful, and His names denote pure perfection without an opposing defect; the Imams describe Him as rich, living, and mighty unlike creatures bearing those traits.
TABATABAI:17:110/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى غني لا كالأغنياء، حي لا كالأحياء، عزيز لا كالأعزة

TABATABAI:17:110/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:110/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:110/r3.claim: The pronoun in the promise that He has the beautiful names refers to the transcendent divine essence, not to either spoken name; any of His names is a path of invocation to Him.
TABATABAI:17:110/r3.anchor: والضمير في قوله { أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى } عائد إلى الذات المتعالية من كل اسم ورسم

TABATABAI:17:110/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:110/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:110/r4.claim: The verse rejects pagan worship of names or their angelic and jinn manifestations: though pagans profess one supreme essence, they direct worship to its supposed offspring and manifestations.
TABATABAI:17:110/r4.anchor: فإن الوثنية - على ما تقدم جملة من آرائهم في الجزء العاشر من الكتاب - ترى أنه سبحانه ذات متعالية من كل حد ونعت ثم تعينت بأسماء اسما بعد اسم

TABATABAI:17:110/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:110/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:110/r5.claim: A polytheist mocked the Prophet for invoking Allah and al-Raḥmān after forbidding worship of two gods, illustrating that mistaken doctrine.
TABATABAI:17:110/r5.anchor: لما سمع بعض المشركين دعاءه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في صلاته يا الله يا رحمن قال

TABATABAI:17:111/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111/r1.claim: Divine names belong wholly to God and only guide worship toward Him; invoking several names therefore does not divide worship or let a name veil its referent.
TABATABAI:17:111/r1.anchor: فدعاء الأسماء الكثيرة لا ينافي توحيد عبادة الذات كما يمتنع أن تقف العبادة على الاسم ولا يتعداه

TABATABAI:17:111/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111/r2.claim: Calling angels or jinn God's children is mistaken because it implies shared nature or perfection; they and all causes are servants who act only through power God grants and retains ownership over.
TABATABAI:17:111/r2.anchor: ما من سبب من الأسباب الفعالة في الكون إلا وهو تعالى الذي ملكه القدرة على ما يعمله

TABATABAI:17:111/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111/r3.claim: Allāh is among the beautiful names: it derives from al-ilāh, meaning the one worshipped, and its use as a proper name does not prevent predicates from being applied to it.
TABATABAI:17:111/r3.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن لفظة الجلالة من الأسماء الحسنى فهو في أصله - الإله - وصف يفيد معنى المعبودية

TABATABAI:17:111/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111/r4.claim: The command not to be excessively loud or quiet calls for a moderate voice in prayer, a practice the Prophet and believers can follow.
TABATABAI:17:111/r4.anchor: بل اسلك فيما بينهما سبيلا وهو الاعتدال وتسميته سبيلا لأنه سنة يستن بها

TABATABAI:17:111#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r1.claim: If ṣalāt means each prayer distributively, each should use moderate volume; more likely it means the prayers collectively, with audible recitation in dawn, sunset, and night prayers and quiet recitation in the others, as established in practice.
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r1.anchor: وأما لو أريد المجموع ولعله الأظهر كان المعنى لا تجهر في صلواتك كلها ولا تخافت فيها كلها

TABATABAI:17:111#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r2.claim: Audibility reflects God's transcendence and quietness His nearness; using both modes across the prayers honors all the divine names.
TABATABAI:17:111#2/r2.anchor: فالجهر بالصلاة يناسب كونه تعالى عليا متعاليا والإخفاف يناسب كونه قريبا أقرب من حبل الوريد

TABATABAI:17:101-111/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r4.claim: A report says the verse was revealed after Meccan polytheists objected to the Prophet invoking Allah and al-Raḥmān as though they were two gods; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this report best fits the verse among differing occasion reports.
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمكة ذات يوم فدعا الله فقال في دعائه يا الله يا رحمن

TABATABAI:17:101-111/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r5.speaker: هشام بن الحكم
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r5.claim: Asked about God's names, al-Ṣādiq says Allah derives from ilāh, the name differs from the named, and worshipping the name alone is disbelief while treating name and meaning as two objects is polytheism.
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r5.anchor: عن هشام بن الحكم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن أسماء الله عز ذكره واشتقاقها

TABATABAI:17:101-111/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r6.speaker: ابن رئاب
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r6.claim: Al-Ṣādiq distinguishes disbelief in worshipping an imagined God or a name alone, polytheism in worshipping name and meaning together, and true faith in worshipping the meaning through God's attributes.
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r6.anchor: عن ابن رئاب عن غير واحد عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من عبد الله بالتوهم فقد كفر

TABATABAI:17:101-111/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r7.speaker: إبراهيم بن عمر
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r7.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq describes a hidden divine name and a name formed through letters but lacking ordinary description, speech, body, color, dimensions, or limits; three parts were manifested for creation.
TABATABAI:17:101-111/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم بن عمر عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الله تبارك وتعالى خلق اسما بالحروف غير منعوت

TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r1.claim: The report says the revealed forms Allah, Tabārak, and Subḥān each have four pillars, yielding twelve, with thirty derivative names per pillar and 360 beautiful names; the three names veil the one hidden name.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r1.anchor: فالظاهر هو الله وتبارك وسبحان لكل اسم من هذه أربعة أركان فذلك اثنا عشر ركنا

TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r2.claim: Words called God's names are names of names; the realities they indicate are the essence considered with attributes. Essential positive names are identical with the essence, while actional or negative names are additional; spoken labels are created and distinct.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r2.anchor: إنما هي أسماء الأسماء وأن ما تدل عليه وتشير إليه من المصداق أعني الذات مأخوذه بوصف ما هو الاسم بحسب الحقيقة

TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r3.claim: Some early theologians confused divine names with the spoken labels and claimed the name is the named; the two preceding reports reject that equation.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r3.anchor: بعض الجهلة من متكلمي السلف خلطوا بين الأسماء وأسماء الأسماء فحسبوا أن المراد من عينية الأسماء مع الذات

TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r4.claim: The pagan doctrine that worship reaches only names and their angelic or jinn manifestations is also rejected: the verse directs invocation to God Himself.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#2/r4.anchor: والثانية ما عليه الوثنية وهو أن الله سبحانه لا يتعلق به التوجه العبادي وإنما يتعلق بالأسماء

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r1.claim: The preceding report explains how names arise from the transcendent essence and makes clear that it concerns divine names themselves, not the spoken names of names.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r1.anchor: صريح في أن المراد بالأسماء فيها هي الأسماء دون أسماء الأسماء

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r2.speaker: زرارة
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r2.claim: A report from al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet recited aloud in Mecca, enabling polytheists to locate and harm him, so the instruction about prayer volume was revealed.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r2.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r3.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits a similar occasion report from Ibn ʿAbbās; reports from ʿĀʾisha instead connect the verse to supplication, or to tashahhud, and the supplication report does not conflict.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r3.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r4.speaker: سماعة
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq defines whispering as a voice below the hearer's hearing and loud recitation as raising the voice strongly, supporting the author's first interpretation.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r4.anchor: قال المخافتة ما دون سمعك والجهر أن ترفع صوتك شديدا

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r5.claim: Al-Ṣādiq tells an imam to recite at a middle volume so that even a large congregation can hear, citing the verse.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r5.anchor: فقال ليقرأ وسطا يقول الله تبارك وتعالى { ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها }

TABRISI:17:109-110/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:109-110/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the occasion was the Prophet’s nighttime prostration in Mecca, calling God al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm; polytheists mocked that he invoked two gods.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r2.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ساجدا ذات ليلة بمكة يدعو يا رحمن

TABRISI:17:109-110/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
TABRISI:17:109-110/r3.claim: Maymūn b. Mihrān says polytheists objected that they knew al-Raḥīm but not al-Raḥmān.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r3.anchor: أن المشركين قالوا أما الرحيم فنعرفه وأما الرحمن فلا نعرفه

TABRISI:17:109-110/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:17:109-110/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jews objected that the Qurʾān mentions al-Raḥmān less often than the Torah.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r4.anchor: أن اليهود قالوا إن ذكر الرحمن في القرآن قليل وهو في التوراة كثير

TABRISI:17:109-110/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:109-110/r5.claim: Any of God’s names may be invoked because all are beautiful; “or” permits either or both names, and mā either reinforces ayyan or means any thing.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r5.anchor: أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى

TABRISI:17:109-110/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:109-110/r6.claim: Names of divine essence include Living, Knowing, and Powerful; names for good acts include Creator, Provider, Just, and Merciful; al-Ṣamad describes servants turning to God for needs.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r6.anchor: فأما أسماؤه المنبئة عن صفات ذاته فهو القادر العالم الحي السميع

TABRISI:17:109-110/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:109-110/r7.claim: The verse establishes one God despite varied names and attributes, recommends invoking beautiful names before petitions, and supports that He does no evil or injustice.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r7.anchor: بين سبحانه في هذه الآية أنه شيء واحد وإن اختلفت أسماؤه وصفاته

TABRISI:17:109-110/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:17:109-110/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the command as avoiding public recitation around those who would harm the Prophet, while not suppressing it around those seeking to hear.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r8.anchor: لا تجهر بإشاعة صلاتك عند من يؤذيك ولا تخافت بها عند من يلتمسها منك

TABRISI:17:109-110/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:109-110/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:17:109-110/r9.claim: A report says pagans heard the Prophet’s loud prayer, abused him, and caused harm, so he was told not to recite aloud; this was early in Mecca.
TABRISI:17:109-110/r9.anchor: كان إذا صلى فجهر في صلاته تسمع له المشركون فشتموه وآذوه

TABRISI:17:110-111/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:110-111/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء ومكحول
TABRISI:17:110-111/r1.claim: Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and Makḥūl, with a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbās, take ṣalāt to mean supplication: neither call loudly nor whisper.
TABRISI:17:110-111/r1.anchor: أن معناه لا تجهر بدعائك ولا تخافت بها ولكن بين ذلك

TABRISI:17:110-111/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:110-111/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:17:110-111/r2.claim: Abū Muslim says not to make all prayer loud or quiet: recite night prayers aloud and daytime prayers quietly.
TABRISI:17:110-111/r2.anchor: بأن تجهر بصلاة الليل وتخافت بصلاة النهار عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:17:110-111/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:110-111/r3.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:17:110-111/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says not to recite so loudly as to distract nearby worshippers or so softly that one cannot hear oneself.
TABRISI:17:110-111/r3.anchor: لا تجهر جهرا يشغل به من يصلي بقربك ولا تخافت بها

TABRISI:17:110-111/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:110-111/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:17:110-111/r4.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh defines loudness as forceful voice and quietness as inaudibility to one’s own ears, recommending a middle recitation.
TABRISI:17:110-111/r4.anchor: الجهر بها رفع الصوت شديدا والمخافتة ما لم تسمع أذنيك

TABRISI:17:110-111/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:110-111/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:110-111/r5.claim: The wording says between “that” in the singular because the reference is to the act, as in 2:68.
TABRISI:17:110-111/r5.anchor: ولم يقل بين ذينك لأنه أراد به الفعل

THALABI:v6p141/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p141/r2.claim: The verse was revealed after Muhammad prayed at night and invoked Allah, Rahman, and Rahim in prostration; polytheists alleged he invoked two gods and associated Rahman with Musaylima of Yamama.
THALABI:v6p141/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تهجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة فجعل يقول في سجوده:

THALABI:v6p141/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
THALABI:v6p141/r3.claim: Muhammad first wrote ‘In Your name, O God’; after the basmala in Solomon’s letter was revealed he wrote the full basmala, prompting Arabs to ask what al-Rahman meant.
THALABI:v6p141/r3.anchor: قال ميمون بن مهران: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في أول ما أوحي إليه يكتب:

THALABI:v6p141/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r4.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p141/r4.claim: People of Scripture objected that Muhammad mentioned al-Rahman little although the Torah uses the name often; the verse was revealed in response.
THALABI:v6p141/r4.anchor: الضحاك: قال أهل الكتاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن

THALABI:v6p141/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p141/r5.claim: Whichever of these two names—or any of God’s names—one invokes, the Most Beautiful Names belong to Him; ayyāmanā means ‘whichever you invoke.’
THALABI:v6p141/r5.anchor: أيا ما تدعوا من هذين الاسمين ومن جميع أسمائه فله الأسماء الحسنى

THALABI:v6p141/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p141/r6.claim: Muhammad’s loud recitation let polytheists hear and insult the Quran, its sender, and reciter; the middle course lets companions hear without exposing him to abuse.
THALABI:v6p141/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى بأصحابه رفع صوته بالقرآن،

THALABI:v6p141/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141/r7.speaker: سعيد
THALABI:v6p141/r7.claim: Muhammad used to recite aloud in the Sacred Mosque; Quraysh asked him not to do so lest he offend their gods and threatened to revile his Lord.
THALABI:v6p141/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر بقراءة القرآن في المسجد الحرام،

THALABI:v6p141#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p141#2/r1.claim: At Abu Sufyan’s house near Safa, Abu Jahl told Muhammad not to fabricate about God; when Muhammad lowered his voice, Abu Jahl boasted he had silenced him, prompting the revelation.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r1.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي في دار أبي سفيان بن حرب عند الصفا،

THALABI:v6p141#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
THALABI:v6p141#2/r2.claim: Abu Bakr whispered to privately address God, while Umar recited loudly to drive away Satan and awaken the Lord; the verse made Abu Bakr raise his voice slightly and Umar lower his.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r2.anchor: وروى [علقمة] عن ابن سيرين في هذه الآية قال: كان أبو بكر

THALABI:v6p141#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v6p141#2/r3.claim: She says the verse concerned the tashahhud, when a Bedouin recited it loudly.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r3.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي (رضي الله عنه) : نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد،

THALABI:v6p141#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p141#2/r4.claim: Do not use prayer publicly for show, nor neglect it in private.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: [لا تراء] بصلاتك في العلانية ولا [تسئها] في السر.

THALABI:v6p141#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r5.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p141#2/r5.claim: The command means neither pray ostentatiously before people nor abandon prayer out of fear of them.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r5.anchor: الوالبي عن ابن عباس: لا تصل مرائيا الناس، ولا تدعها مخافة الناس،

THALABI:v6p141#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p141#2/r6.claim: People of Scripture whispered so softly no letter was heard; God forbids shouting like them or whispering like them, and Gabriel taught the middle way in prayer.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r6.anchor: ابن زيد: كان أهل الكتاب يخافتون في الصلاة، لم يجهر أحدهم بالحرف

THALABI:v6p141#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r7.speaker: علي والنخعي ومجاهد وابن مكحول
THALABI:v6p141#2/r7.claim: They apply the command to supplication rather than ritual recitation.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r7.anchor: وقال: علي والنخعي ومجاهد وابن مكحول: هي في الدعاء

THALABI:v6p141#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
THALABI:v6p141#2/r8.claim: When Bedouins of Banu Tamim asked God for provision after Muhammad’s prayer, he asked whether they were shouting, and the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن شداد: كان أعراب من بني تميم إذا سلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v6p141#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r9.speaker: شيخ من أصحاب رسول الله
THALABI:v6p141#2/r9.claim: A Companion says the verse concerns supplication: do not raise the voice while seeking forgiveness; recall sins quietly so others do not hear and repeat them.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r9.anchor: أن شيخا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثه أن رسول الله قال في هذه الآية:

THALABI:v6p141#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p141#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p141#2/r10.claim: Khafata can describe a dead person when the body has cooled; the prescribed course lies between loudness and whispering.
THALABI:v6p141#2/r10.anchor: ومنه يقال للميت إذا برد خفت. وابتغ بين ذلك أي بين الجهر والإخفات سبيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed one night saying 'O Most Merciful'; Abu Jahl, unfamiliar with that name, accused him of calling a second deity, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال وهو ساجد ذات ليلة:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r2.claim: The command tells the Prophet to invite the polytheists to call either Allah or al-Rahman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r2.anchor: أي: قل يا محمد: ادعوا الله يا معشر المشركين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r3.claim: Calling God by either name returns to one referent; whichever of God's beautiful names they use, they call upon Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أعلمهم الله أن دعاءهم الله ودعاءهم الرحمن يرجعان إلى واحد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r4.claim: Calling Allah or al-Rahman invokes one God, not two.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r4.anchor: وقال المبرد: يقول إذا دعوتم الله الرحمن فإنما تدعون واحدا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r5.claim: The grammarians distinguish three uses of ay: interrogative, conditional, and declarative; interrogative and conditional uses need no relative clause and are governed by what follows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p510/r5.anchor: قال النحويون: (أي) في الكلام تقع في ثلاثة مواضع؛ أحدها: الاستفهام،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r1.claim: Zuhayr's line uses the feminine form ayatan when it is not annexed, meaning 'which direction they went.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r1.anchor: يراد أية وجهة، فانثها حين لم يضفها؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r2.claim: Mā in ayyan mā is an expletive particle, as in the cited examples; tadʿū is jussive after conditional ay, and the fāʾ introduces the answer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r2.anchor: و (ما) في قوله: {أيا ما} صلة، كقوله: {جند ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r3.claim: The Prophet recited loudly and the polytheists insulted him and the Qur'an; he was told not to be loud enough for them to hear and insult, or so quiet his companions could not hear, but to let them hear at times.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r3.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال: (كان رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r4.speaker: قتادة والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r4.claim: They report the same occasion: the Prophet's loud recitation led the polytheists to insult the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r4.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة والسدي (¬2)، واختيار أبي إسحاق،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r5.claim: He prefers the middle course: avoid exposing the Qur'an to their insults without whispering so softly that the companions cannot hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r5.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة والسدي (¬2)، واختيار أبي إسحاق، قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r6.claim: The passage explains khafata as weakening or quieting a voice, with related uses for dying, wilting crops, reciting softly, and private discussion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p511/r6.anchor: يقال: خفت صوته يخفت خفوتا وخفاتا،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r3.claim: The Prophet called on Allah and al-Rahman; Abu Jahl heard and accused him of worshipping two gods while invoking another deity named al-Rahman, prompting the revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: يا الله، يا رحمان، فسمع ذلك أبو جهل فقال: إن محمدا ينهانا أن نعبد إلهين،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r4.claim: Believers may call on God as Allah or al-Rahman; whichever name they invoke, the most beautiful names belong to Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r4.anchor: { قل } يا محمد { ادعوا الله } يا معشر المؤمنين { أو ادعوا الرحمن } إن شئتم قولوا: يا الله وإن شئتم قولوا: يا رحمان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r5.claim: Here, ‘prayer’ means recitation; it should not be so loud that polytheists hear and insult the Qur’an.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r5.anchor: { ولا تجهر بصلاتك } بقراءتك فيسمعها المشركون فيسبوا القرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r6.claim: Do not recite so quietly that companions cannot hear; choose a middle way between loudness and softness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:109-110/r6.anchor: { ولا تخافت بها } ولا تخفها عن أصحابك فلا تسمعهم { وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r5.claim: The polytheists said they knew Allah but did not know al-Raḥmān, so God commanded the Prophet to call upon either name.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r5.anchor: وذلك أن المشركين قالوا: أما الله فنعرفه، وأما الرحمن فلا نعرفه، فقال الله:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r6.claim: Allah and al-Raḥmān are the same God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: أي أنه هو الله وهو الرحمن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r7.claim: The expression أيّا ما تدعوا is in the language of the Kalb tribe and means whichever name you invoke.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p167/r7.anchor: قرة بن خالد، عن قتادة، قال: هي بلسان كلب. يقول: تدعوا أي الاسمين دعوتموه به.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r1.claim: The beautiful names include Allah and al-Raḥmān, whom disbelievers reject while the Prophet says, “He is my Lord.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r1.anchor: وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r2.claim: Allah and al-Raḥmān are names reserved to God that no creature can claim for itself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r2.anchor: أبو الأشعث، عن الحسن، قال: الله والرحمن اسمان ممنوعان، لا يستطيع أحد من الخلق أن ينتحلهما.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r3.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r3.claim: In Mecca, the Prophet prayed with companions; loud recitation let polytheists hear and harm him, while quiet recitation kept followers from hearing, so he was ordered to take a middle course.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r3.anchor: تفسير الكلبي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ هو بمكة كان يجتمع إليه أصحابه، فإذا صلى بهم ورفع صوته سمع المشركون صوته فآذوه، وإن خفض صوته لم يسمع من خلفه، فأمره الله أن يبتغي بين ذلك سبيلا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r4.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet should avoid being heard by polytheists, who would insult him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد في حديث الأعمش: حتى لا يسمعك المشركون فيسبوك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r5.claim: In Mecca, polytheists answered the Prophet's loud prayer with abuse; he was told to lower and moderate his voice, and what one's ears hear is not whispering.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: كان نبي الله وهو بمكة إذا سمع المشركون صوته رموه بكل خبث، فأمره الله أن يغض من صوته وأن يقتصد في صلاته، وكان يقال: ما أسمعت أذنيك فليس تخافت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r6.claim: Mujahid interprets prayer here as supplication and petition.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r6.anchor: عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} [الإسراء: 110] في الدعاء والمسألة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says some prayers are recited silently and others aloud, so each should be recited according to its prescribed mode.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r7.anchor: ابن لهيعة، عن عبد الله بن هبيرة، أن ابن عباس كان يقول: إن من الصلاة سرا، ومنها جهرا، فلا تجهر فيما تسر فيه، ولا تسر فيما تجهر فيه،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r8.claim: Yahya adopts Ibn Abbas's explanation: recite aloud in prayers prescribed aloud and quietly in prayers prescribed quietly.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r8.anchor: قال يحيى: هي على هذا التفسير: أي تجهر فيما يجهر فيه وتسر فيما يسر فيه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r9.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r9.claim: In a report from Zayd ibn Aslam, the Prophet approved Abu Bakr's quiet prayer, Umar's loud prayer, and Bilal's switching surahs, then directed each to moderate or complete his recitation; the verse was revealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p168/r9.anchor: عثمان، عن زيد بن أسلم، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع أبا بكر وهو يصلي من الليل وهو يخفي صوته، وسمع عمر وهو يجهر صوته،

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r1.claim: When the Prophet prayed in Mecca using both Allah and Rahman, polytheists accused him of worshipping two gods, and this command was revealed in response.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r1.anchor: “yâ Allah yâ Rahmân” diye dua ederken müşrikler işitmişler

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r2.claim: Allah's beautiful names express the highest beauty, majesty, and generosity, and prayer using any of them is permissible.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r2.anchor: En yüksek cemâl ve celâl ve ikram ifade eden Esmâ-i Hüsnâ hep O’nundur.

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r3.claim: Having many names does not entail multiple named beings; invoking all the beautiful names is still prayer to the one God without partner.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r3.anchor: ismin ta‘addüdünden müsemmânın ta‘addüdü lâzım gelmez.

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r4.claim: Prayer recitation or supplication should not be shouted, lest it suggest ostentation or disrespect.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r4.anchor: namazda kıraat veya dua ederken bağırma; gösteriş, saygısızlık şâibesi olmasın

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
