ELMALILI:17:110-111/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r5.claim: It should not be so quiet that one cannot hear oneself, as though afraid of others; the right way is between the extremes.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r5.anchor: işitmeyecek kadar da gizleme, mâsivâdan korkuyormuş gibi olmasın

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r13.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet recited this surah and Surah al-Zumar every night.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r13.anchor: bu sûre ile Sûre-i Zümer’i her gece okurdu.

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r14.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet called this surah and the following ones among his earliest treasures and old possessions, meaning early Meccan revelations and treasured memorized devotions.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r14.anchor: İbn Mes‘ud’dan rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûl-i Ekrem bu sûre ile bunu tâkip eden Kehf, Meryem, Tâ-Hâ, Enbiyâ sûreleri hakkında buyurmuştur ki

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r15.claim: He reads the sequence from Isra's promise of the Praised Station to Anbiya's declaration that Muhammad was sent as mercy as deliberately ordered on that basis.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r15.anchor: tebcîline müntehî olan Sûre-i Enbiyâ’ya kadar bu beş sûrenin tertîbi de bu esas üzeredir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r1.speaker: Taberî; Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r1.claim: A report says polytheists heard Muhammad invoke God as Allah or al-Rahman and spread the rumor that he worshipped two gods; the verse permits invoking God by any beautiful name.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r1.anchor: putperestlerden biri Hz. Peygamber’in “ey Allahım!, ey rahmân!” veya “yâ rahmân, yâ rahîm” şeklinde farklı isimlerle dua ettiğini duyunca, “Muhammed iki tanrıya tapıyor” diyerek dedikodu yapmaya başlamışlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r2.claim: Since Arabs already recognized one supreme creator by both names, opponents likely knew the rumor would have little effect; the likelier concern was whether Muslims could keep using names such as al-Rahman.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r2.anchor: Muhtemelen müslümanların eskiden kullandıkları rahmân gibi ilâhî isimleri bundan sonra da kullanıp kullanamayacakları hususunda tereddüt göstermeleri üzerine bu açıklama yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r3.speaker: unnamed report
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r3.claim: One report takes salat here as prayer: Muhammad recited aloud with his companions in Mecca, and the verse instructed him to moderate his voice after polytheists insulted the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r3.anchor: Hz. Peygamber Mekke’de ashabıyla namaz kılarken âyetleri yüksek sesle okur, onun okuyuşunu duyan müşrikler Kur’an’a hakaret ederlerdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r4.speaker: Hz. Âişe ve Ebû Hüreyre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r4.claim: They are cited for understanding salat here to mean supplication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r4.anchor: Hz. Âişe ve Ebû Hüreyre’ye isnad edilen diğer bir rivayete göre salât kelimesi burada “dua” anlamındadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r5.speaker: unnamed view
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r5.claim: Another view takes raising the voice to refer to noon and afternoon prayers and lowering it to the other prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r5.anchor: “Sesini fazla yükseltme!” derken öğle ve ikindi namazlarının, “sesini fazla da kısma” derken diğer namazların kastedildiği görüşü de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r6.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r6.claim: He interprets the instruction as not raising the voice while reciting Qur’an, supplicating, asking the Lord, or remembering Him, lest polytheists hear and distress Muhammad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r6.anchor: Taberî, bu görüşlere dair rivayetleri geniş olarak aktardıktan sonra âyete şu mânayı vermektedir: “Ey Muhammed! Namazında Kur’an okurken, dua ederken, rabbinden dilekte bulunurken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r7.claim: Because nearby verses discuss Qur’an recitation and supplication and verse 111 gives a prayer, salat may encompass both supplication and recitation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:110/r7.anchor: salât kelimesinin dua ve kıraat anlamlarını birlikte içerdiği de düşünülebilir.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet prayed in Mecca and invoked Allah and al-Rahman, polytheists mocked him for supposedly calling two gods, prompting the verse permitting either name.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ذات يوم فدعا فقال في دعائه يا الله يا رحمن فقال المشركون انظروا إلى هذا الصابىء

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that while secretly in Mecca the Prophet recited aloud in prayer; polytheists insulted the Qur'an, its revealer, and its bearer, prompting the instruction not to recite too loudly or too quietly.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ قال نزلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مختف بمكة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r4.speaker: عائشة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r4.claim: Aisha reports that the instruction not to recite too loudly or quietly concerned supplication; Ibn Jarir also transmits a similar report from Ibn Abbas.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r4.anchor: وأخرج البخاري أيضا عن عائشة أنها نزلت في الدعاء

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r5.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r5.claim: Suyuti and Nawawi prefer the first, stronger-chain explanation; Ibn Hajar says both can be reconciled if the supplication occurred inside prayer, supported by a report from Abu Hurayra about prayer at the Kaaba.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r5.anchor: ثم رجح الأولى لكونها أصح سندا وكذا رجحها النووي وغيره وقال الحافظ ابن حجر لكن يحتمل الجمع بينهما بأنها نزلت في الدعاء داخل الصلاة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r6.speaker: عائشة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r6.claim: Aisha reports that the verse concerned the tashahhud, clarifying her earlier report about supplication.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير والحاكم عن عائشة قالت نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people used to loudly pray for mercy, so they were ordered neither to whisper nor to raise their voices.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p141/r7.anchor: ولابن منيع في مسنده عن ابن عباس كانوا يجهرون بالدعاء اللهم ارحمني فنزلت فأمروا أن لا يخافتوا ولا يجهروا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Meccan polytheists objected when the Prophet invoked al-Raḥmān alongside Allah, claiming they knew only Musaylima, called the Raḥmān of Yamāma.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تهجد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذات ليلة بمكة، فجعل يقول في سجوده: يا رحمن يا رحيم، فقال المشركون:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r4.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r4.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān says that after 27:30 prompted the Prophet to write “In the name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful,” Arabs said they knew al-Raḥīm but not al-Raḥmān, prompting this verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r4.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يكتب في أول ما يوحى إليه: باسمك اللهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says People of the Book told the Prophet that al-Raḥmān was mentioned often in the Torah but little by him, and this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p294/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: قال أهل الكتاب لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وقد أكثر الله في التوراة هذا الاسم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the instruction to moderate recitation came while the Prophet was hidden in Mecca: loud recitation let polytheists hear and curse it, while quiet recitation kept his companions from hearing. Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قال: نزلت ورسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مختف بمكة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r2.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the verse concerned the tashahhud, when a Bedouin would recite the prayer's words loudly.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r2.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد، كان الأعرابي يجهر فيقول: التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād says Bedouins of Banū Tamīm would loudly ask God for wealth and children after the Prophet's prayer, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن شداد: كان أعراب من بني تميم إذا سلم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من صلاته قالوا: اللهم ارزقنا مالا وولدا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r4.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha gives another explanation, saying this verse was revealed concerning supplication.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p295/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في قوله تعالى: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} قالت: إنها نزلت في الدعاء

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r1.claim: Ayyan is the object of tadʿū, with the omitted genitive understood as “which of the two names”; it also makes the verb jussive.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r1.anchor: " أيا " منصوب ب " تدعوا " على المفعول به، والمضاف إليه محذوف، أي: أي الاسمين

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r2.claim: The nominal clause fa-lahu al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā is the answer; the proposed omitted answer jāza followed by a new clause is rejected.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r2.anchor: والجواب الجملة الاسمية من قوله { فله الأسمآء الحسنى }. وقيل: هو محذوف تقديره: جاز

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r3.claim: The tanwīn on ayyan substitutes for the omitted genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r3.anchor: والتنوين في " أيا " عوض من المضاف إليه

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r4.claim: Mā is either an emphatic extra particle or a condition repeated for emphasis, like repeated prepositions; a poetic line illustrates the latter.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r4.anchor: وفي " ما " قولان، أحدهما: أنها مزيدة للتاكيد. والثاني: أنها شرطية جمع بينهما تأكيدا

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r5.claim: An anonymous poetic line illustrates the doubled construction cited as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r5.anchor: فأصبحن لا يسألنني عن بما به

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r6.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r6.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads ayyan man tadʿū, supporting the debate over whether the particle is extra or conditional.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r6.anchor: ويؤيد هذا ما قرأ به طلحة بن مصرف " أيا من تدعوا "

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r7.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi allows man to be an extra particle, as in the cited poetic usage.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r7.anchor: فقيل: " من " تحتمل الزيادة على رأي الكسائي

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r8.claim: The two readers stop on ayyan by changing its tanwīn to alif and continue through mā; other readers stop on mā because it fuses with ayyan.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r8.anchor: ووقف الأخوان على " أيا " بإبدال التنوين ألفا، ولم يقفا على " ما " تبيينا لانفصال

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r9.claim: A conditional parse that stops on ayyan is rejected: mā does not refer to individual rational beings, conditionals require generality, and both parts would be omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r9.anchor: وهذا مردود بأن " ما " لا تطلق على آحاد أولي العلم، وبأن الشرط يقتضي عموما، ولا يصح هنا

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r10.claim: Tadʿū can mean invoke, taking one object, or name, taking two objects, the second introduced by a preposition that can be omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r10.anchor: و " تدعوا " هنا يحتمل أن يكون من الدعاء وهو النداء فيتعدى لواحد، وأن يكون بمعنى التسمية فيتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the verb to mean “name,” so the sense is to invoke the deity by whichever of the two names is used.
SAMIN-DURR:17:110/r11.anchor: وممن ذهب إلى كونها بمعنى " سمى " الزمخشري

ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r4.claim: When Arabs heard the name al-Raḥmān, they thought the call invoked two beings; al-Raḥmān is also a name found in earlier revealed scriptures.
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r4.anchor:
لما سمعت العرب ذكر الرحمن قالت: أتدعونا إلى اثنين إلى الله وإلى
الرحمن. واسم الرحمن في الكتب الأول المنزلة على الأنبياء.

ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r5.claim: Calling God or al-Raḥmān addresses the same one; ayyan mā means whichever of God’s beautiful names you invoke.
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r5.anchor: فأعلمهم الله أن دعاءهم الرحمن ودعاءهم الله يرجعان إلى شيء واحد فقال: (أيا ما تدعوا) المعنى أي أسماء الله تدعوا (فله الأسماء الحسنى).

ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r6.claim: Mukhāfata means quiet speech and jahr means raising the voice; the Prophet was told not to expose Qur’anic recitation to the polytheists’ abuse, nor to make it inaudible to companions praying behind him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r6.anchor: فأمره الله - جل وعز - ألا يعرض القرآن لسبهم، وألا يخافت بها مخافتة لا يسمعها من يصلي خلفه من أصحابه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r7.claim: Seek a course between loud recitation and quiet recitation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p264/r7.anchor: أي اسلك طريقا بين الجهر والمخافتة.

ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r1.claim: Al-asma al-husna means the most perfect or goodly names.

ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r2.claim: Ar-Rahman is exclusive to God and denotes the unconditional, all-embracing exercise of grace and mercy.
ASAD-NOTES:17:109#n132/r2.anchor: denoting the unconditional, all-embracing quality and exercise of grace and mercy, and is applied exclusively to God

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p221#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p221#2/r1.claim: Idʿū is read with ḍamma or kasra; the author refers readers to the earlier discussion in al-Baqarah.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: يقرأبالضم والكسر وقد ذكر في البقرة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p384/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p384/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p384/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr transmitters differ over the vowels on lām and wāw; ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza use kasra on both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p384/r5.anchor: 25 قوله ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن ﴾ 110

QIRAAT-ER:17:110:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:1#1/r1.claim: Ḍamma instead of kasra on the final lām is a phonetic liaison difference with no semantic impact.
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:1#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with ḍamma instead of kasra on final lam; purely phonetic liaison difference

QIRAAT-ER:17:110:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:4#1/r1.claim: The ḍamma instead of kasra is a phonetic liaison difference and does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:17:110:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with ḍamma instead of kasra -- phonetic liaison difference only

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r6.speaker: بعض أهل المدينة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r6.claim: Some Medinan authorities say the instruction not to recite aloud was abrogated by the command to remember God inwardly.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r6.anchor: سماك بن الفضل عن بعض أهل المدينة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ﴾ قال هو منسوخة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet used to raise his voice in prayer and be pelted with filth, so he was told to avoid both harmful loudness and whispering and take a middle course.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفع صوته في الصلاة فيرمى بالخبث

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r2.speaker: عروة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r2.claim: ʿUrwa says the instruction concerns supplication.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r2.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه في قوله ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ قال في الدعاء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan warns against making one's public worship look good while one's inward state is bad.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p392#2/r3.anchor: قال معمر وكان الحسن يقول لا تحسن علانيتها وتسيء سريرتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r23.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r23.claim: خافت بالكلام means to whisper so softly that the speaker can barely hear it; خفت of a blow means its sound disappeared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r23.anchor: خافت بالكلام أسره بحيث لا يكاد يسمعه المتكلم وضربه حتى خفت أي لا يسمع له حس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet prayed at night in Mecca, invoking al-Rahman and al-Rahim in prostration; pagans alleged he worshipped two gods, so the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تهجد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة بمكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r6.speaker: مكحول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya transmits a similar account from Makhul about the pagans hearing the Prophet invoke al-Rahman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r6.anchor: ونقل ابن عطية نحوا منه عن مكحول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r7.claim: A second Ibn Abbas account says pagans heard يا الله يا رحمن and again thought he invoked two gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r7.anchor: وقال عن ابن عباس: سمعه المشركون يدعو يا الله يا رحمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r8.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r8.claim: Maimun says the Prophet used باسمك اللهم until revelation of Solomon's letter, then wrote the basmala; Arabs knew al-Rahim but not al-Rahman, prompting this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r8.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: كان عليه السلام يكتب: باسمك اللهم حتى نزلت إنه من سليمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says People of the Book objected that al-Rahman was common in Torah but rare in the Prophet's speech; the verse answered their denial after they failed to match the Quran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: قال أهل الكتاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r10.claim: After being unable to answer the Quran's challenge, opponents accused the Messenger of doing what he forbade by invoking two gods; God answers that charge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126/r10.anchor: وكان عليه الصلاة والسلام قد جاءهم بتوحيد الله والرفض لآلهتهم عدلوا إلى رميه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.claim: The reported occasions of revelation suggest الدعاء here is vocative invocation; Allah and al-Rahman are two names of one referent, one His name and the other His attribute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى: إن دعوتم الله فهو اسمه وإن دعوتم الرحمن فهو صفته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.claim: He takes دعاء as naming rather than calling upon, a verb that can take two objects with one omitted when understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى التسمية لا بمعنى النداء وهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.claim: دعوت may take a direct object and a second complement with باء, which can be omitted; a cited line from Amr's mother illustrates this usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.anchor: ودعوت هذه من الأفعال التي تتعدى إلى اثنين ثانيهما بحرف جر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r4.claim: They treat Allah and al-Rahman as names of the same deity, so either name may be used in invocation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r4.anchor: المراد بهما اسم المسمى وأو للتخيير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r5.claim: أيما is conditional; its tanwin may replace an omitted genitive, while ما may instead be emphatic or itself conditional.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r5.anchor: وأي هنا شرطية. والتنوين قيل عوض من المضاف وما زائدة مؤكدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r6.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r6.claim: He reads أيا من تدعو; من may be redundant by al-Kisa'i's analysis or an anomalous pairing of two conditional particles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف. أيا من تدعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in فله refers to the single referent behind both names, who possesses the most beautiful names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r7.anchor: والضمير في فله عائد على مسمى الاسمين وهو واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r8.claim: A proposed pause after أي treats ما as a new universal conditional, but the author rejects it because ما does not refer to rational individuals and the conditional scope fails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r8.anchor: وهذا لا يصح لأن ما لا تطلق على آحاد أولي العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r9.claim: They interpret صلاة in the command about voice as supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r9.anchor: والصلاة هنا الدعاء قاله ابن عباس وعائشة وجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r10.claim: Another Ibn Abbas view takes صلاة as Quran recitation in ritual prayer, with an understood noun because loudness and whispering concern voice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p126#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: هي قراءة القرآن في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r1.claim: The Prophet raised his Quran recitation and pagans insulted and disrupted it, so he was told to lower it enough not to be heard by them but loud enough for believers behind him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r1.anchor: وكان عليه الصلاة والسلام يرفع صوته بقراءته فيسب المشركون ويلغون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r2.claim: The middle way means a moderate volume between loudness and whispering.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r2.anchor: وابتغ بين ذلك أي بين الجهر والمخافتة سبيلا وسطا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r3.claim: They give the expression a further moral sense: do not make the outward practice good while making its private side bad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والحسن: لا تحسن علانيتها وتسيء سريتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r4.speaker: عائشة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r4.claim: Aisha says صلاة here means the tashahhud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r4.anchor: وعن عائشة: الصلاة يراد بها هنا التشهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r5.claim: Ibn Sirin says the verse concerned Bedouins who said the tashahhud aloud; Abu Bakr whispered to commune with God, while Umar recited aloud to repel Satan and wake sleepers, then each was told to adjust his volume.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r5.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: كان الأعراب يجهرون بتشهدهم فنزلت الآية في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r6.claim: Another Ibn Abbas gloss says not to recite loudly in daytime prayer or whisper in night prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: المعنى ولا تجهر بصلاة النهار ولا تخافت بصلاة الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd relates the verse to Torah and Gospel practice of sometimes raising the leader's voice and sometimes lowering it so followers become silent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p127/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معنى الآية على ما يفعله أهل الإنجيل والتوراة

BURHAN:v3p164/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p164/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p164/r6.claim: Here duʿāʾ means naming: call Him Allah or al-Rahman; otherwise one-object invocation would imply either shirk or naming the same deity twice.
BURHAN:v3p164/r6.anchor: على أن الدعاء بمعنى التسمية التي تتعدى إلى مفعولين أي سموه الله أو سموه الرحمن

BURHAN:v3p147/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p147/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p147/r2.claim: Prayer in the instruction not to be too loud or quiet means the recitation of the prayer.
BURHAN:v3p147/r2.anchor: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ 3 أي بقراءة صلاتك ولا تخافت بقراءتها

BURHAN:v2p502/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p502/r1.claim: The pattern faʿlān is more emphatic than faʿīl; al-Raḥmān is thus more emphatic than al-Raḥīm, with faʿlān marking fullness as in غضبان.
BURHAN:v2p502/r1.anchor: أما فعلان فهو أبلغ من فعيل ومن ثم قيل الرحمن أبلغ من الرحيم وإن كانت صيغة فعيل

BURHAN:v2p502/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p502/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains a poet’s use of raḥmānan for a human as arising from unbelief and obstinacy.
BURHAN:v2p502/r2.anchor: فهو من كفرهم وتعنتهم كذا أجاب به الزمخشري

BURHAN:v2p502/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p502/r3.claim: Some reject al-Zamakhsharī’s answer as insufficient: the poet used an indefinite or annexed form, whereas the debate concerns the definite name al-Raḥmān.
BURHAN:v2p502/r3.anchor: ورده بعضهم بأن النعت لايدفع وقوع إطلاقهم

BURHAN:v2p502/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r4.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v2p502/r4.claim: Ibn Mālik says the poet meant one who possesses mercy, not the proper name that became established by common usage.
BURHAN:v2p502/r4.anchor: وأجاب ابن مالك بأن الشاعر أراد لازلت ذا رحمة ولم يرد بالاسم المستعمل بالغلبة

BURHAN:v2p502/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
BURHAN:v2p502/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the Arabs knew the name al-Raḥmān but were ignorant of its attribute, as shown by their asking ما الرحمن rather than من الرحمن.
BURHAN:v2p502/r5.anchor: فقال ابن العربي إنما جهلوا الصفة دون الموصوف ولذلك لم يقولوا ومن الرحمن

BURHAN:v2p502/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p502/r6.speaker: البرزاباذاني
BURHAN:v2p502/r6.claim: Al-Barzabādhānī says al-Raḥmān means the mighty, just king, not merely one characterized by mercy; the cited verses associate the name with majesty, power, protection, self-sufficiency, and universal sovereignty.
BURHAN:v2p502/r6.anchor: وذكر البرزاباذاني أنهم غلطوا في تفسير الرحمن حيث جعلوه بمعنى المتصف بالرحمة قال وإنما معناه الملك العظيم العادل

BURHAN:v3p207/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p207/r5.claim: Here duʿāʾ means naming, not calling out: the sense is name Him Allah or name Him al-Raḥmān, with the verb taking two objects.
BURHAN:v3p207/r5.anchor: فإنه قد يظن أن الدعاء فيه بمعنى النداء فلا يقدر في الكلام حذف وليس كذلك

BURHAN:v3p76/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p76/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p76/r4.claim: Non-kāffah mā occurs after a jussive particle, as in the construction أيًّا ما تدعوا.
BURHAN:v3p76/r4.anchor: وغير الكافة تقع بعد الجازم نحو

BURHAN:v4p408/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p408/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p408/r2.claim: Mā in the third category accompanies قَلَّ and طال, as in the examples قلما تقولين and طالما تشتكين.
BURHAN:v4p408/r2.anchor: والثالث كقولك قلما تقولين وطالما تشتكين

BURHAN:v4p408/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p408/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p408/r3.claim: A fourth use makes a word operative in a conditional construction when it would not govern by itself, as with إذا and حيث.
BURHAN:v4p408/r3.anchor: والرابع المسلطة وهي التي تجعل اللفظ متسلطا بالعمل بعد إن لم يكن عاملا

BURHAN:v4p408/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p408/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p408/r5.claim: The final use is emphatic mā, which some call a particle of connection and others an extra; the author prefers connection because no Qur’anic particle is meaningless. It occurs medially or finally, between tightly linked elements, and never initially.
BURHAN:v4p408/r5.anchor: لأنه ليس في القرآن حرف إلا وله معنى

ITQAN:v4p437/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p437/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p437/r2.claim: Al-Sabuni transmits from Ibn Abbas, as a raised report, that reciting “Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful” through the surah’s end protects against theft.
ITQAN:v4p437/r2.anchor: من حديث ابن عباس مرفوعا ( هذه الآية أمان من السرق ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن ﴾ إلى آخر السورة

ITQAN:v3p39/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p39/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p39/r2.claim: Another ordering device delays the more eloquent term; examples include al-Rahman before al-Rahim, al-Raʾuf before al-Rahim, and “messenger, prophet,” commonly to preserve the verse ending.
ITQAN:v3p39/r2.anchor: ومن هذا النوع تأخير الأبلغ وقد خرج عليه تقديم

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham distinguishes omission for brevity, where context supplies the object, from omission for restricting attention to the action, where no object is intended and there is no true ellipsis.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام جرت عادة النحويين أن يقولوا بحذف المفعول اختصارا واقتصارا ويريدون بالاختصار الحذف لدليل

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r2.claim: The rhetoricians distinguish mentioning only that an event occurred, without identifying its agent or patient, from construing a verb as having no object for the purpose at hand.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r2.anchor: والتحقيق أن يقال يعني كما قال أهل البيان تارة يتعلق الغرض بالإعلام بمجرد وقوع الفعل من غير تعيين

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r3.claim: When the point is simply the agent’s action, the object is neither stated nor implied; examples include God giving life and death, knowing, eating, drinking, and seeing.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r3.anchor: فيقتصر عليهما ولا يذكر المفعول ولا ينوى إذ المنوى كالثابت ولا يسمى محذوفا

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r5.claim: When the intended construction connects an action to both agent and object, both are expressed; if the object is omitted in this class, it is understood as ellipsis.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r5.anchor: وتارة يقصد إسناد الفعل إلى فاعله وتعليقه بمفعوله فيذكران نحو ﴿ لا تأكلوا الربا ﴾ ﴿ ولا تقربوا الزنى ﴾

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r7.claim: The wording may mean either call upon Allah or al-Rahman, with no omitted object, or name Allah or al-Rahman, with an object understood; the passage leaves the analysis open.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r7.anchor: وقد يشتبه الحال في الحذف وعدمه نحو ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن ﴾

ITQAN:v2p460#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r1.claim: Ayy may be conditional, as in whichever of the two terms I fulfill and whichever name you call upon; the latter is the present verse.
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r1.anchor: الأول أن تكون شرطية نحو ﴿ أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي ﴾

ITQAN:v2p514/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p514/r1.claim: The particle mā can negate while governing like laysa; al-Suyuti says the Qur’an has no fourth instance beyond the three cited constructions.
ITQAN:v2p514/r1.anchor: نافية إما عاملة عمل ليس نحو ﴿ ما هذا بشرا ﴾ ﴿ ما هن أمهاتهم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p514/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p514/r2.claim: Mā can also negate without governing, as in the cited statements about spending and a failed trade.
ITQAN:v2p514/r2.anchor: أو غير عاملة نحو ﴿ وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله ﴾ ﴿ فما ربحت تجارتهم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p514/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r3.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ITQAN:v2p514/r3.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says mā negates the present; al-Sibawayh’s account suggests it adds emphasis because it answers qad, which itself emphasizes an affirmative.
ITQAN:v2p514/r3.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب وهي لنفي الحال ومقتضى كلام سيبويه أن فيها معنى التأكيد لأنه جعلها في النفي جوابا لقد في الإثبات

ITQAN:v2p514/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p514/r4.claim: Mā can be added emphatically as a particle-cancelling element, as in innamā and similar forms.
ITQAN:v2p514/r4.anchor: وزائدة للتأكيد إما كافة نحو ﴿ إنما هو إله واحد ﴾ ﴿ أنما إلهكم إله واحد ﴾

ITQAN:v2p514/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p514/r5.claim: Mā may instead be added without cancelling governance; the verse’s ayyan mā is one of these examples.
ITQAN:v2p514/r5.anchor: أو غير كافة نحو ﴿ فإما ترين ﴾ ﴿ أيا ما تدعوا ﴾ ﴿ أيما الأجلين قضيت ﴾

ITQAN:v2p514/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r6.speaker: الفارسي
ITQAN:v2p514/r6.claim: Al-Farisi says conditional forms following immā are reinforced by the nūn because mā resembles the emphatic lām of an oath.
ITQAN:v2p514/r6.anchor: قال الفارسي جميع ما في القرآن من الشرط بعد إما مؤكد بالنون

ITQAN:v2p514/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
ITQAN:v2p514/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa says adding mā signals a stronger degree of emphasis.
ITQAN:v2p514/r7.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء زيادة ما مؤذنة بإرادة شدة التأكيد

ITQAN:v2p343/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r23.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r23.claim: Seek a middle course between loud and quiet recitation: do not make it excessively loud or so soft that your own ears cannot hear it.
ITQAN:v2p343/r23.anchor: 2200 ﴿ وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا ﴾ اطلب بين الإعلان والجهر وبين التخافت والخفض طريقا لا جهرا شديدا ولا خفضا لا يسمع أذنيك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r1.claim: In the cited poem, a definite predicate is fronted, but the meaning shows it is intended as delayed; otherwise its initial position would make it the subject.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r1.anchor: وإنما دل على أنه ينوي التأخير المعنى ، ولولا ذلك لكانت المعرفة إذا قدمت هي المبتدأ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r2.claim: In the verse, ادعوا means call Him by a name, as one says someone is called Zayd or the amir; it does not mean supplicate to two beings.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r2.anchor: ليس المعنى في ' ادعوا ' الدعاء ، ولكن الذكر بالاسم كقولك : هو يدعى زيدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r3.claim: The omitted wording is ‘call Him Allah or call Him al-Raḥmān’; the selector أي requires alternatives, so a literal reading risks wrongly positing two objects of worship.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r3.anchor: وأن في الكلام محذوفا ، وأن التقدير : قل أدعوه الله ، أو ادعوه الرحمن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r4.claim: Because wording can be interpreted through different implicit structures without changing its words, sound interpretation requires rhetorical knowledge; a surface reading here could lead to shirk.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p281/r4.anchor: وهو الذي وسع مجال التأويل والتفسير ، حتى صاروا يتأولون في الكلام الواحد تأويلين أو أكثر

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r1.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean worship; the command to call upon either divine name means to worship.
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r1.anchor: الدعاء بمعنى العبادة فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r6.claim: The beautiful names mean God’s attributes, including knowledge, power, hearing, sight, will, speech, and life.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r6.anchor: الثالث : الاسم يعني الصفة قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r11.claim: Ṣalāt in the instruction not to recite loudly or too quietly means Qurʾānic recitation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r11.anchor: والخامس : القراءة . ومنه قوله تعالى في بني إسرائيل :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p284/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p284/r1.claim: In this verse, أيًّا ما تدعوا means أيًّا تدعوا; ما is an added particle after أيًّا.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f3.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f3.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes مهما as ما joined to another redundant ما, by analogy with متى ما، إن ما، أينما and أيًّا ما; Quran 17:110 exemplifies the last pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f3.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن مهما فقال هي ما

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنعلامةالمضمرينالمنصوبينإيا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنعلامةالمضمرينالمنصوبينإيا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنعلامةالمضمرينالمنصوبينإيا.claim: Separate accusative pronouns use the form إيا when a corresponding attached suffix is unavailable; where a suffix can attach, speakers use it instead.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنعلامةالمضمرينالمنصوبينإيا.anchor: لأنهم استغنوا بها عن إيا كما استغنوا بالتاء وأخواتها في الرفع

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: أيّ, whether annexed or independent, behaves like من; the verse’s independent أيا ما تدعو is good Arabic, just as the annexed construction is.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.anchor: قال الله عز وجل ^ ( أيا ما تدعو فله الأسماء الحسنى ) ^ فحسن كحسنه مضافا

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: In أيها تشاء لك, تشاء completes أي as a relative clause like الذي; the conditional version may use a jussive, with the construction changing when فاء is supplied. من behaves similarly.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.anchor: فتشاء صلة لأيها حتى كمل اسما ثم بنيت لك على أيها

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: If bare أي were treated as a definite relative pronoun like its annexed form, Sībawayh says it would take no tanwīn when definite and would take tanwīn when indefinite.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.anchor: بمنزلة الذي معرفة أن لا ينون

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: أبي وأيك كان شرا means which of me and you was worse: the two do not share one أي, but each person is considered separately.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: Sībawayh cites al-Abbas ibn Mirdas’s line فأيى ما وأيك كان شرا as evidence for the paired أي construction asking which of two was worse.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: خداش بن زهير
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: Khidash ibn Zuhayr’s line أيي وأيكم أعز وأمنع attests the paired construction meaning which one of me and you is stronger and more protected.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنأيامضافاوغيرمضافبمنزلةمن|.claim: Sībawayh cites Khidash ibn Zuhayr’s second line فأيي وأى ابن الحصين as another attestation of the same distributive أي construction.

NASHR:v2p463/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASHR:v2p463/r1.claim: The Prophet says to call on God while certain of an answer and with an attentive heart; al-Tirmidhī transmits it, and al-Ḥākim calls its chain sound.
NASHR:v2p463/r1.anchor: لحديث أبي هريرة يرفعه " ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة.

NASHR:v2p463/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASHR:v2p463/r2.claim: Another report from Abū Hurayra says to make one's request great, since nothing is too great for God; it is recorded by Muslim, Ibn Ḥibbān, and Abū ʿAwāna.
NASHR:v2p463/r2.anchor: وعنه يرفعه أيضا " إذا دعا أحدكم فليعظم الرغبة

NASHR:v2p463/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p463/r3.claim: A report raised from Ibn ʿAbbās recommends supplicating with the palms and wiping the face afterward; it is narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Ḥākim in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
NASHR:v2p463/r3.anchor: لحديث ابن عباس يرفعه " إذا سألتم الله فسلوه ببطون أكفكم،

NASHR:v2p463/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r4.speaker: السائب بن يزيد عن أبيه
NASHR:v2p463/r4.claim: Al-Sāʾib b. Yazīd reports from his father that the Prophet raised his hands in supplication and wiped his face; Abū Dāwūd records it.
NASHR:v2p463/r4.anchor: وعن السائب بن يزيد عن أبيه - رضي الله عنهما - أن النبي

NASHR:v2p463/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r5.speaker: عمر
NASHR:v2p463/r5.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet did not lower raised hands after supplication until wiping his face; al-Ḥākim records it in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Tirmidhī calls it sound in some copies.
NASHR:v2p463/r5.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه قال:

NASHR:v2p463/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r6.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
NASHR:v2p463/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām rejected wiping the face after supplication in his fatwas; Ibn al-Jazarī says he likely had not encountered these hadiths.
NASHR:v2p463/r6.anchor: ورأيت بعض علمائنا، وهو ابن عبد السلام في فتاواه

NASHR:v2p463/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p463/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī recounts seeing the Prophet in a vision during a crisis in 792 AH; he asked for supplication for himself and the Muslims, and the Prophet prayed and wiped his face.
NASHR:v2p463/r7.anchor: أنا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في شدة نزلت بي وبالمسلمين

NASHR:v2p463/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p463/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p463/r8.claim: At Qurʾān completion, although some reciters chose fixed personal prayers, Ibn al-Jazarī recommends staying with the Prophet's transmitted supplications because his comprehensive words suffice and provide the model.
NASHR:v2p463/r8.anchor: واختيارنا أن لا يجاوز ما ورد عنه

NASHR:v2p144/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p144/r1.speaker: الداني، وطاهر بن غلبون، وابن شريح
NASHR:v2p144/r1.claim: Al-Dānī, Ṭāhir b. Ghalbūn, and Ibn Shurayḥ report that Hamza and al-Kisāʾī stop on أيّا before ما; Ibn Ghalbūn also notes a Ruways disagreement, while the others stop on ما.
NASHR:v2p144/r1.anchor: أبي عمرو الداني في التيسير، وشيخه طاهر بن غلبون

NASHR:v2p144/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p144/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p144/r2.claim: Most authorities give no specific stop ruling; because أيّا and ما are separate words in the rasm, Ibn al-Jazarī finds both stop points permissible and closest to the governing principles.
NASHR:v2p144/r2.anchor: وهذا هو الأقرب إلى الصواب، وهو الأولى بالأصول

NASHR:v2p144/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p144/r3.speaker: ابن سعدان
NASHR:v2p144/r3.claim: Ibn Saʿdān reports that Hamza and Salīm stop on أيّا, but he considers stopping on ما better because ما is an augmenting particle attached to أيّ.
